Join NTMA
NTMA has the know-how, resources and national presence to drive positive change and growth.
 “Joining the NTMA has been an integral part to the success of JD Machine. I have learned so much, gained valuable relationships in networking with my peers across the country. I truly believe we are stronger together.”
 – Matt Wardle, President & CEO, JD Machine
More than 1,000 strong, our members are small and medium-sized companies, many of them family owned or privately held. They believe in the NTMA, because for more than 80 years, NTMA has been focused on the strength, growth and future of American manufacturing. 
NTMA has the know-how, resources and national presence to drive positive change and growth. We’re shaping the perception of precision manufacturing across the U.S. and people are noticing.
Join us.
Please fill the form below and one of our team members will contact you to get started!
What Members Can Expect
Networking
It’s all about connection. NTMA provides national and local gatherings for you to talk and share with other manufacturers. Join us for a national conference or an Emerging Leaders’ Roundtable. Can’t take time out of your shop? We get it.  You’ll have the chance to meet virtually, too, through webinars and discussion boards. We understand that everyone’s circumstances are different, and we work to create opportunities for you to meet and learn from your peers, industry experts and emerging leaders in whatever way works best for you.
Learn More
Workforce Development
It’s no secret that manufacturing is facing a labor shortage. NTMA is focused on getting ahead of that curve by filling the skills-gap now and in the future. We have a suite of programs targeted at the current workforce and support organizations as well as students, their families and schools. We want to up-skill today’s workers and prepare the next generation of precision manufacturers as they enter the workforce.
Learn More
Advocacy
NTMA is committed to representing our industry in Washington, D.C. — fighting for legislation that builds a strong future for manufacturing. NTMA is an active partner in One Voice, the federal advocacy group that represents small and medium-sized manufacturing businesses in America.
Learn More

My Membership Options
NTMA members are companies that believe in the future of U.S. manufacturing. They are tool and die makers, precision manufacturers, suppliers and supporters. Join us.
Join the largest precision manufacturing trade association in the United States and get an opportunity to collaborate with like-minded professionals who know that a strong manufacturing sector means a strong economy and a strong nation.
We offer three levels of annual membership. Explore membership options below to find the best fit for your organization.
Regular Membership
Any proprietorship, partnership, corporation or other business entity in the United States of America accepting the Association’s Mission, Vision, and Values and primarily engaged in precision custom manufacturing, through tooling or machining, is eligible to become a regular Member. For purposes of this paragraph, “precision custom manufacturing” is defined to include companies engaged in:
Additive machining/manufacturing
Design
Die building
Die building and production
Mold building
Mold building and production
Precision fabricating
Precision machining
Rapid prototyping
Special tooling
Special tooling and production
Special machine building
Special machine building and production
Such other activities as may be approved by the Board of Trustees
Regular Members automatically become members of a local chapter if there is one located in their vicinity. This allows companies to connect regionally to network, collaborate and advocate. Click Here to find a local NTMA chapter and learn more.
National Associate Membership
Any proprietorship, partnership, corporation, or other business entity located in the United States of America and regularly engaged in providing materials, services or supplies to the precision custom manufacturing industry shall be eligible to become a national associate member of this Association. No person, firm, or corporation eligible for membership as a regular member shall be eligible for associate membership.
Academic Memberships
Individual Educators employed in metalworking and technological institutions such as colleges, universities, career technical education programs, or formal online training programs are eligible for individual educator memberships.
Chapter Membership
If you join as a Regular Member you are automatically a member of a local chapter if there is one located in your vicinity.  Click Here for a list of local NTMA Chapters to see if there is one in your area and to learn more about what they have to offer.
Student Membership
New in 2025, an individual interested in taking NTMA-U courses can join NTMA with limited member benefits that include member pricing for all NTMA-U courses and related textbooks.  Student members also can attend NTMA National events at member prices, have access to online issues of The Record as well as NTMA Connect, the Associations online member community.

 FAQS 
 PMA Questions?
 If you don’t see your question listed, feel free to reach out—we’re happy to help! 
 Contact Us
 How do I join PMA? 
 To join PMA, visit the membership page and complete the interest form. You’ll need to provide information about your company and your areas of interest. After submission, a member of PMA’s membership team will follow up with you and schedule a call to learn more. Membership is open to companies in the metalforming industry.
 How much is a yearly membership? 
 The yearly membership fee for PMA varies depending on your company’s size and type. Fees are structured to ensure accessibility for businesses of all sizes, from small manufacturers to large corporations. Contact PMA directly for a customized quote.
 How do I renew? 
 You will be sent your renewal notice via email. The email will contain your invoice and instructions to renew. Renewals typically go out to members in November. Complete the renewal process to ensure continuous access to all the resources and benefits that PMA offers. Renewal reminders are sent before your membership expires.
 Can I attend events if I’m not a member? 
 Nonmembers can attend most PMA events, but they will need to pay at the nonmember registration price, which is typically higher than the discounted rate available to members. PMA members enjoy reduced rates and priority access to these events, making membership a cost-effective option for regular attendees.

 FAQS 
 PMA Questions?
 If you don’t see your question listed, feel free to reach out—we’re happy to help! 
 Contact Us
 How do I join PMA? 
 To join PMA, visit the membership page and complete the interest form. You’ll need to provide information about your company and your areas of interest. After submission, a member of PMA’s membership team will follow up with you and schedule a call to learn more. Membership is open to companies in the metalforming industry.
 How much is a yearly membership? 
 The yearly membership fee for PMA varies depending on your company’s size and type. Fees are structured to ensure accessibility for businesses of all sizes, from small manufacturers to large corporations. Contact PMA directly for a customized quote.
 How do I renew? 
 You will be sent your renewal notice via email. The email will contain your invoice and instructions to renew. Renewals typically go out to members in November. Complete the renewal process to ensure continuous access to all the resources and benefits that PMA offers. Renewal reminders are sent before your membership expires.
 Can I attend events if I’m not a member? 
 Nonmembers can attend most PMA events, but they will need to pay at the nonmember registration price, which is typically higher than the discounted rate available to members. PMA members enjoy reduced rates and priority access to these events, making membership a cost-effective option for regular attendees.

 What is the difference between the Business & Premier Membership?
 With both member levels, ALL employees at that location are eligible for
 membership benefits and discounts. They offer all the same benefits; however, the Premier
 Membership includes one FREE registration to FMA’s Annual Meeting, FREE
 unlimited access to FMA’s Online e-Learning

 Assessment Tool.

 Just the Business or Premier are location specific and will only cover employees at
 that
 location. Whereas the multi-site membership covers up to 5 different locations with each
 additional location after the 5 at just $100 per location.
 If I work remotely, do I need to purchase my own Individual Membership, or can I be covered
 under the company’s membership?
 If you work remotely for your company out of your home, and your company
 already holds an FMA membership, there is no need to purchase your own membership. We will
 just be sure to list you under the company’s record so that you have full access to FMA membership benefits & discounts and will make
 your ship-to address your home address.

 do a search by type of company, state, company name, etc.

 Gunderson regarding our Sponsorship
 opportunities that are available.

 Survey?

 participating FMA
 members do receive the survey results for FREE when they are available.

 Once you have signed up for membership and it is paid for in full, the membership
 is good, and
 you can begin utilizing membership benefits & discounts right away

 online or contact our Customer Service department at 815-399-8700
 or toll free at 888-394-4362.

 User’s Groups, teaching a class, etc.

 Common Questions About ISA:
 What does MROP mean in industrial supply?
 MROP stands for Maintenance, Repair, Operations, and Production. In the industrial supply channel, MROP products include the tools, fasteners, safety equipment, consumables, and indirect materials that keep facilities running, equipment operating, and production moving. The MROP supply chain connects manufacturers, distributors, and end users across industrial, manufacturing, and commercial markets.
 What is the Industrial Supply Association (ISA)?
 The Industrial Supply Association (ISA) is the leading trade association serving the full industrial MROP supply channel. ISA brings together manufacturers, distributors, industrial manufacturers' representatives (IMRs), and industry partners to provide market intelligence, education, peer networks, and live events that help industrial MROP supply channel companies make better decisions, grow performance, and stay competitive in a changing industrial market.
 Who should join the Industrial Supply Association?
 ISA membership is designed for industrial manufacturers, distributors, industrial manufacturers' representatives (IMRs), service providers, and solution partners that support the MROP supply chain. Whether you are a small independent company or a large global organization, ISA is for leaders and teams looking to strengthen relationships, gain industry insights, develop talent, and connect across the full channel.
 How much does ISA membership cost?
 ISA membership pricing varies based on company type, size, and role in the industrial supply channel. Membership is structured to be accessible and scalable, with dues reflecting the value delivered through business intelligence and reporting, education, research, events, and peer engagement. The best way to understand pricing is to connect with the ISA team for a brief conversation about your organization and goals.
 What's the difference between ISA and other industrial groups?
 ISA is the only association built to serve the entire industrial MROP supply channel. We are not focused on a single segment. Instead, we intentionally connect manufacturers, distributors, industrial manufacturers' representatives (IMRs), and industry partners to strengthen performance across the full channel.
This full-channel perspective gives companies what they actually need to lead in a changing market: clearer insight, stronger relationships, and strategies that work across organizations. It’s how we expand impact, deepen collaboration, and position the industry for long-term success.
It’s how ISA continues Leading the Channel Forward since 1902.

 Frequently Asked Questions
 How many people in my company can access ISA benefits once we join?
 Everyone. ISA membership is enterprise-wide, giving every employee across your organization and locations access to industry reports, economic forecasts, peer networks, analytics tools, webinars, our on-demand learning library, and the membership directory at no additional cost. Certifications, sales training, and in-person events are available at exclusive member pricing.
 What if I have questions before applying?
 Schedule a fit conversation with our team anytime. Email us at info@isapartners.org.
 What does MROP stand for? 
 MROP stands for Maintenance, Repair, Operations, and Production, the products and supplies that keep industrial facilities running. ISA is the trade association built specifically for the manufacturers, distributors, and reps who make up this channel.
 What is the Industrial Supply Association (ISA)? 
 The Industrial Supply Association (ISA) is a 120+ year-old trade association serving the full industrial MROP channel (manufacturers, distributors, reps, and service providers) with market intelligence, training, peer networks, and events across North America.
 How much does ISA membership cost? 
 Dues are structured by company type and annual revenue, so pricing scales fairly for organizations of every size. The fastest way to get an exact number is a quick dues assessment call with our membership team.
 Who should join the Industrial Supply Association?
 Any company in the industrial MROP supply chain - distributors, manufacturers, IMRs, and service providers, from independent shops to global organizations - looking to strengthen channel relationships, sharpen strategy with real market data, and develop talent.
 Is ISA membership worth it for smaller distributors or manufacturers? 
 Yes. ISA's enterprise-wide structure means smaller companies get the same access to market intelligence, training, and peer networks as the largest members in the channel... often the fastest way for a lean team to compete with much bigger ones.
 What's the difference between a distributor, manufacturer, and industrial manufacturers' rep (IMR)?
 Distributors buy MROP products from manufacturers and sell to end users. Manufacturers produce the products sold through the channel. Industrial manufacturers' reps (IMRs) represent manufacturers and support sales at the distributor level. ISA is the only association connecting all three as equal stakeholders.

Our Story
The National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors (NAW) is one of America’s leading trade associations and the national voice of the $8.6 trillion wholesale distribution industry, the backbone of the supply chain, that supports more than 6 million jobs and powers nearly one-third of the U.S. economy. Founded in 1946, NAW represents industry trade associations and companies spanning every sector of distribution.
NAW’s Voice in Washington, DC
At the core of NAW’s mission is advocacy. NAW champions policies that strengthen free enterprise, protect the supply chain, promote economic growth, and ensure wholesale distributors have a strong voice in Washington and state capitals across the country. Through government relations, public affairs, and the NAW Legal Policy Center, NAW works to advance the interests of distributors and defend the critical role they play in the American economy and way of life.

Types of Memberships
 Full Member
This membership class includes manufacturers in the plastics supply chain. Full member sub-categories include:
Equipment Manufacturers & Moldmakers: Manufacturers of plastics processing equipment, including primary machinery, secondary auxiliaries, molds, dies, tools, spare parts, and other components.
Material Suppliers: Manufacturers and compounders of raw materials such as resins, fillers, stabilizers, pigments and other components, including bioplastics and recycled materials.
Processors/Converters: Manufacturers of plastic products through injection molding, blow molding, thermoforming, extrusion, transfer molding, compression molding and other methods.
 Associate Member
Associate members are companies that stock and sell products manufactured by third parties that are utilized by processors in the production of any plastics products. Associate member sub-categories include: 
Distributor: Third party sales of raw materials, equipment, molds, or plastics products.
Manufacturer Representative or Sales Agent: Individual entities reselling products for principal manufacturers of raw materials, equipment, molds, or plastic products.
 Service Provider
Publishers, researchers, consultants and any other corporation that devotes a significant portion of its business to the plastics industry can join PLASTICS as service providers.
This includes but is not limited to banks, insurance agencies, software development companies, utilities, logistics, transportation, testing services and state economic development agencies, as well as individuals engaged in educational and governmental research or professional pursuits directly related to the development or use of plastics.
View our PLASTICS membership brochure to see all member benefits and resources available to members.

Kim McLoughlinSenior Research Engineer, Global Materials ScienceBraskem
×
A Resin Supplier’s Perspective on Partnerships for the Circular Economy
About the Speaker
Kim drives technology programs at Braskem to develop advanced polyolefins with improved recyclability and sustainability. As Principal Investigator on a REMADE-funded collaboration, Kim leads a diverse industry-academic team that is developing a process to recycle elastomers as secondary feedstock. Kim has a PhD in Chemical Engineering from Cornell. She is an inventor on more than 25 patents and applications for novel polyolefin technologies. Kim is on the Board of Directors of SPE’s Thermoplastic Materials & Foams Division, where she has served as Education Chair and Councilor.
Close
Gamini Mendis, Ph.D.Assistant Professor, Plastics Engineering TechnologyPenn State Erie, The Behrend College
×
A Resin Supplier’s Perspective on Partnerships for the Circular Economy
About the Speaker
Gamini has a BS and PhD from Purdue University in Materials Engineering and Sustainability. He joined Penn State as a Post Doctorate Scholar in 2020 prior to his professorship appointment. He works closely with PA plastics manufacturers to implement sustainability programs in their plants. 
Close
Tom GiovannettiTechnical Service Engineer, Injection and Rotational Molding and CAEChevron Phillips Chemcial Company
×
A Resin Supplier’s Perspective on Partnerships for the Circular Economy
About the Speaker
Tom Giovannetti holds a Degree in Mechanical Engineering from The University of Tulsa and for the last 26 years has worked for Chevron Phillips Chemical Company. Tom started his plastics career by designing various injection molded products for the chemical industry including explosion proof plugs and receptacles, panel boards and detonation arrestors for 24 inch pipelines. Tom also holds a patent for design of a polyphenylene sulfide sleeve in a nylon coolant cross-over of an air intake manifold and is a Certified Plastic Technologist through the Society of Plastic Engineers. Tom serves on the Oklahoma Section Board as Councilor, is also the past president of the local Oklahoma SPE Section, and as well serves on the SPE Injection Molding Division board.
Close
Joseph Lawrence, Ph.D.Senior Director and Research ProfessorUniversity of Toledo
×
A Resin Supplier’s Perspective on Partnerships for the Circular Economy
About the Speaker
Dr. Joseph Lawrence is a Research Professor and Senior Director of the Polymer Institute and the Center for Materials and Sensor Characterization at the University of Toledo. He is a Chemical Engineer by training and after working in the process industry, he has been engaged in polymers and composites research for 18+ years. In the Polymer Institute he leads research on renewably sourced polymers, plastics recycling, and additive manufacturing. He is also the lead investigator of the Polyesters and Barrier Materials Research Consortium funded by industry. Dr. Lawrence has advised 20 graduate students, mentored 8 staff scientists and several undergraduate students.  He is a peer reviewer in several journals, has authored 30+ peer-reviewed publications and serves on the board of the Injection Molding Division of SPE.
Close
Matt HammernikNortheast Account ManagerHasco America
×
A Resin Supplier’s Perspective on Partnerships for the Circular Economy
About the Speaker
Matt Hammernik serves as Hasco America’s Northeast Area Account Manager covering the states Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky.  He started with Hasco America at the beginning of March 2022. Matt started in the Injection Mold Industry roughly 10 years ago as an estimator quoting injection mold base steel, components and machining. He advanced into outside sales and has been serving molders, mold builders and mold makers for about 7 years.

Where Do You Fit In?
Member Type?*Member Type *ManufacturerSupplierDistributorAffiliateInternational
Manufacturer: Any person, company or corporation engaged in the manufacture of composites products that are sold into the composites supply-chain,
including reinforced polymer composites or cast polymer, that perform composites manufacturing processes, including but not limited to hand lay-up,
spray-up, compression molding, pultrusion, vacuum infusion processing, or other variations of manufacturing processes.
 View PDF Application Form
Supplier: Any person, company or corporation engaged in the manufacture of equipment (including machines and tooling), materials (including resin,
fiber, additives, molding compound, prepreg), manufacturing aides and supplies, or processing services (including recycling, post-mold finishing) to the
composites industry.
 View PDF Application Form
Distributor: Any person, company or corporation engaged in the distribution of equipment, materials, manufacturing aides and supplies, or services to
the composites industry, and who does not meet the definition of supplier.
 View PDF Application Form
Affiliate: Any person, company or corporation not eligible for regular or associate membership in the association, including sole proprietorship consultants, publications, professional and trade associations, end users and other non-profit organizations that service the composites industry. Affiliate members have no voting rights in the Association.
 View PDF Application Form
International: Any person, company or organization with operations and headquarters outside of North America engaged in the manufacture or distribution of equipment to
manufacture composite products (including machines and tooling), materials for producing composite products (including resin, fiber, additives, compounds, prepreg, manufacturing aides, supplies, technology or processing services) and/or composite products themselves.

Membership Awards
The ACMA Awards recognize outstanding members for their dedication and hard work to ensure that the composites industry prospers.
2026 ACMA MEMBERSHIP AWARD RECIPIENTS & 2027 CRITERIA
The ACMA Awards recognize excellence, leadership, and innovation within the composites industry. These awards honor individuals and organizations that have made lasting contributions in various areas, from technical advancements to industry leadership.
Below are the 2026 award recipients for each category as well as the 2027 eligibility & criteria for nomination:
 Don MasseyVectorply
LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT AWARD
The ACMA Lifetime Achievement Award recognizes a business owner who has been in the composites industry for at least 20 years and, through their involvement, has made a significant and lasting contribution to the industry.
This award is sponsored by Superior Huntingdon Composites
 Don Massey Biography minus plus 
Don Massey is the founder and former CEO of Vectorply Corporation. He began his career in IT at Playtex in Dover, Delaware, before relocating to Columbus, Georgia, to work for Swift Denim. He advanced into senior leadership and ultimately served as Executive Vice President of Sales, overseeing denim sales worldwide. During this time, he developed experience in sales leadership, customer relationships, and business growth.
In the late 1980s, Massey accepted an early retirement package and began a consulting career. One of his first clients was Johnston Industries, a traditional textile manufacturer with a stitch-bond division that primarily produced polyester materials for liner applications. He was asked to investigate Fiberglass Non-Crimp Stitched Reinforcements, an emerging technology within the composites industry.
Massey spent six months researching composites applications, manufacturing requirements, performance needs, and market opportunities. Based on his findings, he recommended that Johnston Industries invest in and diversify into the composites industry. This work marked the beginning of his long-term involvement in the composites industry and preceded his founding of Vectorply Corporation.
 2026 Eligibility & Criteria minus plus 
The ACMA Lifetime Achievement Award recognizes a business owner who has been in the composites industry for at least 20 years and, through their involvement, has made a significant and lasting contribution to the industry.
Nominees must have demonstrated lasting and outstanding contributions in one or more of the following areas:
Exemplary contribution to legislative and/or regulatory affairs of significant long-term consequence to the industry.
Invention of a process or product that has significant long-term importance.
A very successful business career in which measurable contributions have been made to industry, government, employees, or the community.
Leadership throughout their career to the industry’s trade associations where lasting contributions were made, including SPI, SIRC, NMMA, ACMA, etc.
Additional Considerations
Previous recipients of the Pioneer Award are eligible for this honor.
Sitting members of the ACMA Board are not eligible for consideration.
Submit a nomination
 Dustin TroutmanCreative Composites Group
HALL OF FAME AWARD
The ACMA Hall of Fame Award recognizes a member who has attained distinction among peers through their efforts, involvement, and accomplishments in the composites industry and its associations.
This award is sponsored by Vectorply Corporation
 Dustin Troutman Biography minus plus 
Dustin Troutman received his Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering from University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown in 1993. He currently serves as Chief Sales Officer for Creative Composites Group. 
With more than 30 years at CCG, Mr. Troutman has been instrumental in market development, product innovation, and the sales growth of major pultrusion products for infrastructure and custom applications. His leadership has supported the advancement of product lines including SUPERPILE™ pipe piles, SuperLoc® sheet piles, and StormStrong® FRP transmission and distribution poles, among others. 
He remains actively involved in the development of industry codes and standards supporting the fiberglass-reinforced polymer (FRP) pultrusion industry. Mr. Troutman is a co-inventor on six patents related to pultruded structural systems. 
Mr. Troutman is a member of professional organizations including American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE), American National Standards Institute (ANSI), and ASTM International (ASTM). He is a past President of the Pultrusion Industry Council and currently serves as Chair of the Utility and Communication Structures Committee. Additionally, he served on the Project Advisory Committee (PAC) responsible for developing the ASCE/LRFD standard for pultruded structural profiles.
 2027 Eligibility & Criteria minus plus 
The ACMA Hall of Fame Award recognizes a member who has attained distinction among peers through their efforts, involvement and accomplishments in the composites industry and its associations.
Nominees must have demonstrated outstanding contributions in one or more of the following areas:
Contribution to legislative and/or regulatory affairs of significant long-term consequence to the industry.
Invention of a process or product which has commercial value to the composites or cast polymer industry.
A successful business career in which notable contributions have been made to the composites industry.
Participation in the industry’s trade associations, including SPI, SIRC, ACMA, etc.
Academic contributions that have resulted in a noteworthy impact on the composites industry.
Additional Considerations
Previous recipients of the SPI Clare E. Bacon Award or the Pioneer Award are eligible for this honor.
Sitting members of the ACMA Board are not eligible for induction into the Hall of Fame.
ACMA staff are eligible for induction into the Hall of Fame.
Submit a nomination
 Kevin Q. WalshUniversity of Notre Dame / Frost Engineering & Consulting
ACADEMIC PIONEER AWARD
The Academic Pioneer Award has been created to recognize original, visionary, and innovative ideas that have been scientifically investigated, tested, and demonstrated to advance composites technology.
This award is sponsored by Champion Fiberglass
 Kevin Q. Walsh Biography minus plus 
Dr. Kevin Quinn Walsh is a structural engineering professional whose practice, research, and standards work center on the design, testing, and codification of pultruded fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) structural systems into the built environment. He is a Principal at Frost Engineering & Consulting in Mishawaka, Indiana (FROST), one of the only structural design firms in the world that regularly designs and specifies loadbearing structures with pultruded FRP. He is concurrently a faculty member in the University of Notre Dame Department of Civil & Environmental Engineering & Earth Sciences, where he directs the professional Master of Engineering (MEng) program. 
Dr. Walsh designs or serves as the Engineer of Record (EOR) or QA/QC Engineer across the commercial, industrial, multi-residential, educational, medical, data center, and public infrastructure sectors, including on more than 200 pultruded FRP projects. This work runs through FROST’s advanced materials portfolio and includes projects such as (but not limited to) FRP industrial and data center structures, residential building systems, bridges, deep foundation piles, and the experimental testing of novel FRP members and framing connections. He has held Professional Engineer (PE) or Structural Engineer (SE) registration in 25 states. 
Dr. Walsh has been the principal investigator behind a sustained line of FRP experimental testing funded by industry partners addressing adhered semi-rigid beam-to-column connections, LRFD resistance-factor calibration for bolted FRP frames, novel long-span profiles, material testing with parametric loading vectors, and elevated-temperature performance. Dr. Walsh contributes to design-standards development, committee work, and funded research with the American Composites Manufacturers Association (ACMA), the ACI Center of Excellence for Nonmetallic Building Materials (NEx), and the Institute for Advanced Composites Manufacturing Innovation (IACMI). He has also served previously on ASCE and ASTM committees. He has published more than 35 peer-reviewed journal articles alongside scores of conference papers and technical reports. 
Dr. Walsh earned a Bachelor of Civil Engineering from the University of Dayton, a Master of Science in Civil Engineering from the University of Notre Dame, and a Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from the University of Auckland, New Zealand. His broader interests span resilient infrastructure, lightweight structures, seismic assessment of historic buildings, large-scale testing of in situ structures, masonry buildings, and unbonded post-tensioning systems. At Notre Dame, he primarily teaches senior and graduate design courses, including Lightweight Structural Materials, Structural Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering, Structural Masonry Assessment and Design, Historic Preservation, Structural Wood Design, Principles of Practice, and Design Capstone. He received the 2023 Rev. Edmund P. Joyce, C.S.C., Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching.
 2027 Eligibility & Criteria minus plus 
The Academic Pioneer Award has been created to recognize original, visionary, and innovative ideas that have been scientifically investigated, tested, and demonstrated to advance composites technology.
Nominees must be academic professionals who have demonstrated outstanding contributions in one or more of the following areas:
As an academic:
Performed fundamental research leading to prototyping of new composite products.
Active in the development of standards, specifications, design guidelines, and codes supporting state-of-the-art practices in new applications.
As a professor:
Educated undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and postdoctoral students in composites technology through course development, instruction, and testing programs.
Authored technical papers, journal articles, educational presentations, book chapters, or books to advance composites technology.
Actively engages the composites industry to promote market development through technical, trade, and professional associations, including but not limited to ACMA.
Submit a nomination
 Jim BonoPolynt Composites USA Inc.
 Lei Zhao Avient Corporation
PIONEER AWARD
The Pioneer Award honors individuals who have played a pivotal role in advancing the composites industry through hands-on innovation, technical expertise, and dedication to excellence. This award recognizes the unsung heroes—the engineers, technicians, craftsmen, and problem-solvers—who have made lasting contributions through their work, often behind the scenes.
This award is sponsored by Composites One
 Jim Bono Biography minus plus 
Jim Bono is an accomplished composites industry professional with more than 35 years of experience in the composites industry. He currently serves as a Technical Manager for Polynt Composites USA Inc., where he has spent the past 18 years supporting the company’s high-temperature resin product line throughout the United States. 
In his role at Polynt (formerly Reichhold), Jim is responsible for the technical development of applications utilizing Polynt resin systems, resin product development, and providing technical support to a broad range of customers. His expertise spans numerous composite manufacturing processes, including Sheet Molding Compound (SMC), Bulk Molding Compound (BMC), Resin Transfer Molding (RTM), Light RTM, prepreg processing, compression molding, injection molding, cast polymers, and pultrusion. He particularly enjoys working directly with customers to address technical challenges, develop solutions, and support the implementation of composite technologies across diverse applications. 
Prior to joining Polynt, Jim spent 19 years with Continental Structural Plastics (formerly ThyssenKrupp Budd), where he managed the company’s SMC compounding facility engineering and quality functions after having worked in R&D on the development of composite products for numerous automotive programs. His contributions included working on many automotive vehicle development platforms which involved the development of new materials and processes. These experiences provided him with a strong foundation in both manufacturing and product development, helping to advance the adoption of composite materials in demanding automotive applications. 
Jim earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry from Oakland University and a Master of Science degree in Macromolecular Chemistry from the University of Detroit Mercy. Demonstrating a lifelong commitment to learning and professional development, he completed his master’s degree while working full time in the composites industry. The combination of academic study and hands-on industry experience provided him with a unique perspective, enabling him to bridge the gap between polymer chemistry and practical manufacturing applications. 
Throughout his career, Jim has been driven by a commitment to continuous learning, innovation, and problem solving. He enjoys tackling complex manufacturing and design challenges, finding practical solutions, and sharing those lessons with colleagues, customers, and industry partners. He believes that some of the most valuable professional experiences come from collaborating with others and learning from the challenges presented by new opportunities. 
Outside of work, Jim enjoys spending time with his family, especially his five grandchildren. He is also an avid runner and gardener, activities that allow him to stay active, maintain balance, and enjoy time outdoors. Whether in his professional or personal life, he values growth, perseverance, and the opportunity to learn something new every day.
 Lei Zhao Biography minus plus 
With 30 years of experience in the composites industry spanning academia, engineering, product development, and manufacturing, Lei Zhao, Ph.D., P.E., is a recognized leader in advanced composite materials and their applications across infrastructure, transportation, energy, marine, and industrial markets. Throughout his career, Lei has combined deep technical expertise with practical business insight to drive innovation, develop high-performance material solutions, and mentor the next generation of engineering professionals.
Since 2014, Lei has served as Senior Technology Manager within the Advanced Composites Division of Avient Corporation. In this role, he leads the development, design, and testing of composite material solutions for a wide range of applications. His work is centered on creating customized material solutions that address complex customer requirements while delivering measurable commercial value. Equally committed to organizational growth, he places strong emphasis on developing technical talent and cultivating business acumen among engineering teams, helping align technical innovation with long-term business success.
Prior to joining Avient, Lei spent six years with Gibraltar Industries, where he led the design and fabrication of FRP structures, pultrusion process development, and tooling design. He later expanded his responsibilities to include new product development for both metal and composite products, as well as manufacturing technology development.
Lei began his professional career in academia, holding research and faculty appointments at the University of California, San Diego, and the University of Central Florida. His research focused on the application of fiber-reinforced composites in civil infrastructure systems, advancing the understanding and implementation of composite technologies in construction and structural engineering. As an educator, he taught courses in structural engineering, mechanics, and composite materials.
Lei is a long-standing member of ACMA and its Pultrusion Council and is actively contributing to the ongoing revision of the ACMA FRP Utility Pole Standard Specifications. He previously served on the FRP Bar Grating Committee.
In addition to his involvement with ACMA, Lei is a member of the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) and is a registered Professional Engineer. He formerly served as Chair of the National Association of Architectural Metal Manufacturers (NAAMM) Bar Grating Manual MBG 531 Subcommittee. Lei is credited with five patents covering a range of construction materials and composite technologies.
Lei resides in Birmingham, Alabama, with his wife, Mei Chih, who also studied engineering in her youth. Their daughters, Audrey and Charlene, are also engineers.
 2027 Eligibility & Criteria minus plus 
The Pioneer Award honors individuals who have played a pivotal role in advancing the composites industry through hands-on innovation, technical expertise, and dedication to excellence. This award recognizes the unsung heroes—the engineers, technicians, craftsmen, and problem-solvers—who have made lasting contributions through their work, often behind the scenes.
Nominees must have demonstrated outstanding contributions in one or more of the following areas:
Process & Manufacturing Innovations – Developed or refined manufacturing processes that improved efficiency, quality, or scalability of composite materials.
Material Advancements – Played a key role in formulating, testing, or deploying new composite materials that enhanced performance and expanded industry applications.
Hands-On Engineering & Problem-Solving – Solved critical technical challenges in production, fabrication, or product development that enabled industry progress.
Mentorship & Workforce Development – Trained, mentored, or influenced the next generation of composite professionals through education, training, or knowledge-sharing.
Sustainability & Impact – Contributed to recycling initiatives, waste reduction, or sustainable material solutions within composites manufacturing.
This award is designed for doers, not just decision-makers—the engineers, shop-floor innovators, technicians, and behind-the-scenes contributors whose efforts have shaped the industry. Candidates do not need to hold executive or leadership positions but must have had a measurable impact on composites technology, manufacturing, or industry growth.
Additional Considerations
Candidates must not have been previously recognized as Lifetime Achievement or Hall of Fame award winners.
Pioneer Award recipients will remain eligible for these honors in the future.
Open to individuals across all industry sectors, including R&D, manufacturing, production, and field operations.
Awards can be made posthumously.
Must have worked for a company that is currently or formerly a member of ACMA.
Submit a nomination
 Kelly DeBuskComposites Compliance, LLC
 Scott T. HolmesResilient Structures
OUTSTANDING VOLUNTEER AWARD
Each year, an individual that has gone the extra mile this last year in their service to ACMA and the industry is recognized by ACMA staff and members.
This award is sponsored by Norplex Micarta
 Kelly DeBusk Biography minus plus 
Kelly DeBusk is a seasoned expert with over 27 years of experience in environmental and safety regulations within the composites industry. As the owner of Composites Compliance, LLC, she specializes in guiding small composites companies through the complex regulatory landscape that affects their operations. Her unique background, growing up in a family-owned composites business, has equipped her with essential manufacturing skills that enhance her ability to offer practical and effective regulatory compliance solutions. 
Kelly emphasizes the importance of understanding the manufacturing process to create effective permits and implement robust safety programs. In addition to her consulting work, she has recently stepped into the role of Vice President at her family’s business, Appalachian Plastics, Inc., further cementing her commitment to the industry. 
Passionate about supporting the composites sector, Kelly advocates for businesses to ensure they can meet proposed regulatory standards and voices concerns when new regulations may negatively impact them. She has volunteered her time across the industry with ICPA and ACMA committees and boards to keep the industry informed and actively address new regulations facing it.
 Scott T. Holmes Biography minus plus 
As Chief Technology Officer at Resilient Structures, Mr. Holmes leads the company’s research and development strategy and supports regulatory engagement at the federal and state levels. He also contributes to the advancement and refinement of industry standards. 
Mr. Holmes brings more than 35 years of composites experience across the aerospace, defense, and utility markets, including more than 18 years focused on utility structures. He is dedicated to advancing composite solutions that improve safety, performance, and service life. 
He has been a leading advocate for ACMA and the broader composites industry. As a founding member and former Chair of ACMA’s Utility & Communication Structures Council, he helped advance the adoption of composite materials in the utility market through education, industry engagement, and standards development.  
He currently chairs the committee responsible for the Specification for FRP Composite Utility Poles, which published its first edition in 2019 and is developing an expanded revised edition for publication in 2028. He has also represented ACMA through multiple code cycles of the National Electrical Safety Code (NESC) on the Overhead Lines subcommittee. 
Mr. Holmes has authored more than 40 peer-reviewed technical publications and holds 10 U.S. patents. He earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Delaware.
Nomination ProcessThis award is nominated by ACMA committee members & staff and does not accept external nominations.
Want Your Trophy Ideas!
We’re looking to design a brand-new ACMA Membership Awards trophy for future ceremonies, and we want our members to help us create it. 
If you have an idea for what an ACMA composite trophy could look like, click the link and submit the form. Whether your idea is sleek and modern, creative and unconventional, or something completely unexpected, we want to see it.

 Membership
Membership Opportunities
Why become a NADCA member? NADCA is solely dedicated to the die casting industry, providing members with access to resources and a network of die casting peers that help solve technical, operational and business challenges. And if that’s not enough, how about: 
 Education. 
A comprehensive selection of educational opportunities in a variety of formats that focus on workforce training and business improvement.
 Research & Development. 
A vigorous program that explores new materials and casting processes and manages a comprehensive technical archive.
 Networking and Collaboration. 
A dynamic environment where peers can network and collaborate – learning from each other and sharing valuable best practices. 
 Advocacy. 
Having a reputable voice for the industry, educating audiences – government, OEMs, academia – on the importance and benefits of die casting.
 Benchmarking and Data. 
Facilitating continuous improvement through surveys and market studies to identify best practices, key trends and process and performance benchmarking.
 OEM Resources.
Converting or creating a die cast part? NADCA Design points you to the right suppliers, support materials, engineering consults or even a custom value-analysis seminar. 
 Membership Levels
 Corporate Membership
For any entity (company, partnership, etc.) with a physical presence in North America that is engaged in the manufacturing, design or purchasing of die castings; a supplier to die casting manufacturers; or a manufacturer’s representative or professional consultant working with a NADCA Corporate Member.
Learn More 
 Individual Membership
For individuals participating in or affiliated with the die casting industry.
Learn More  Join Now
Student Membership
For high school or college students in North America.
Learn More 
 Membership Plus
An upgrade for North American-based NADCA members, Membership Plus provides access to engineering tools, software and an online community for business and operational information and resources.
Learn More 
 NADCA Chapters
NADCA's regional Chapters are independently led by volunteers within the die casting industry. In addition to being the regional hub for the die casting industry, the Chapters provide educational and networking opportunities through meetings and events. 
Learn More

What Is Powder Metallurgy?
Powder metallurgy is a metal-forming process performed by heating compacted metal powders to just below their melting points. The technology encompasses multiple processes including conventional powder metallurgy (also known as press-and-sinter), metal injection molding, isostatic pressing, metal additive manufacturing (also known as metal 3D printing), and powder forging.

 Membership Benefits 
Take advantage of opportunities within the growing powder metallurgy and particulate materials markets by joining with other industry companies to promote programs that influence the awareness and expansion of the technology. 
MPIF membership can fine tune your management/marketing strategy by providing you with up-to-date industry news and information.  You will receive the following correspondences:
 Member Briefs Newsletter (MPIF members only): Monthly information related to the Federation and its associations.
 Monthly Economic Indicators (MPIF Members only): This report is generally issued twice a month and is a member's only benefit. The Economic Indicators encompasses leading and lagging indicators for U.S. gross domestic product; automotive sales and production; agriculture; firearms; powder shipments; and U.S., Japanese, and European imports and exports. The full report is updated and stored in the MPIF Members Only section of this website.
 PM Confidence Index (MPIF members only): Compare your business condition with others in the industry.
 FocusPM: Powder Metallurgy News & Information: This is a bi-weekly newsletter with PM industry updates from around the world, including updates on companies, PM industry professionals, and more. 
 Conferences/Seminars/Pubs: Your connection to information regarding PowderMet, Short Course, Standards, etc.
 APMI International West Penn Chapter: If you are located in the St. Mary's, Pennsylvania, area and you're interested in learning more about APMI International and the monthly West Penn Chapter meetings, this is the list for you!
MPIF is able to deal more effectively with industry-wide problems and threats, such as those posed by environmental forces, safety and health regulations, unfair trade practices, or competitive processes/materials. 
Association and Federation income is all member-directed toward support of various programs that influence the awareness and expansion of the technology, such as: 
 management information
 annual technical conferences & exhibits 
 technical and professional education 
 publications 
 industry marketing 
 government relations 
 statistics 
 technology development 
 standards 
 technology transfer 
Member companies participate in committees and boards such as: 
 Roadmap Committee 
 Standards and Statistics Committees 
 Technical Board 
 Industry Development Board 
In addition, each individual association may offer other benefits specific to the needs of its members.
Technical Conferences
Over the course of the year, MPIF offers multiple conferences, seminars, webinars, and the Basic PM Short Course. These events draw in several thousand global PM industry professional to review the latest industry advancements and for professional development.

 In addition to corporate membership in the six associations that make up the Federation, there are three other membership options. 
Corporate Affiliate Membership: Designed for companies that want to be kept abreast of PM technology and industry developments but do not fit within the scope of any of the six associations. 
Associate/Consultant Membership: These members provide a variety of services including development and implementation of new technology, plant setup, part and tool design, laboratory service, market research, quality assessment, injection molding, magnetic applications, personnel training, and research and development programs. 
Associate/Overseas Membership: Companies that are located outside of North America (and are not eligible for membership in an association that accepts overseas members) are eligible for an Associate/Overseas membership. Associate/Overseas members enjoy most of the same benefits of corporate membership except voting privileges.

 What is Anodizing?
 … the Finish of Choice
 Anodizing is an electrochemical process that converts the metal surface into a decorative, durable, corrosion-resistant, anodic oxide finish. Aluminum is ideally suited to anodizing, although other nonferrous metals, such as magnesium and titanium, also can be anodized.

 Aluminum is the Ideal Metal to be used in anodizing
 Anodizing is an electrochemical process that converts the metal surface into a decorative, durable, corrosion-resistant, anodic oxide finish. Aluminum is ideally suited to anodizing, although other nonferrous metals, such as magnesium and titanium, also can be anodized.
The anodic oxide structure originates from the aluminum substrate and is composed entirely of aluminum oxide. This aluminum oxide is not applied to the surface like paint or plating, but is fully integrated with the underlying aluminum substrate, so it cannot chip or peel. It has a highly ordered, porous structure that allows for secondary processes such as coloring and sealing.
Anodizing is accomplished by immersing the aluminum into an acid electrolyte bath and passing an electric current through the medium. A cathode is mounted to the inside of the anodizing tank; the aluminum acts as an anode, so that oxygen ions are released from the electrolyte to combine with the aluminum atoms at the surface of the part being anodized. Anodizing is, therefore, a matter of highly controlled oxidation the enhancement of a naturally occurring phenomenon.

 WHY JOIN AEC?
 Committed to helping its members overcome the challenges that arise in a competitive manufacturing environment, the AEC...
 Educates designers and manufacturers on the advantages and applications of aluminum extrusions.
 Publishes the yearly Buyers' Guide, a directory of member companies to be used as a buyer's resource. Informs members about emerging technologies and industry trends via publications and educational opportunities* such as training sessions, online programs, seminars and conferences.
 Collects, analyzes, and disseminates production and management statistical information to help benchmark operations.
 Works with government and regulatory bodies on matters pertinent to the industry. Offers technical and managerial publications and training events to keep the aluminum extruders knowledgeable of the latest important issues.
 Provides numerous networking opportunities for members to exchange, discuss, and problem-solve their common challenges. Advocates for North American aluminum extrusion industry interests. Listens to members' concerns and allows for member input through various volunteer opportunities.
 Focus
 To serve the aluminum extrusion industry as a whole, AEC extends membership to all those with an active interest in this industry:
 Aluminum Extruders
 Producers of Aluminum Billet
 Suppliers of equipment, products and services for the extrusion industry.
AEC's focus is simply stated, the Aluminum Extruders Council will:
 Expand the market
 Defend the market, and
 Teach its members how to become better extruders.
 Business Excellence
 AEC assists members in the aluminum extrusion industry to be the best they can be and enhances the ability of its members to meet the emerging demands of the market through knowledge sharing and best practices. AEC offers resources for members to continuously improve and excel in their profession, as well as expand their operations. Programs include:
Technical Webinars - Convenient and complimentary educational webinars for training and educating personnel from the convenience of your own offices and plant, available only to AEC members.
Workshops & Clinics - Every year, AEC produces a variety of educational in-person workshops, clinics and classes covering a wealth of topics dedicated to improvement of extrusion operations - from safety and finishing to press maintenance and die performance improvement.
Two Yearly Conferences - Every Spring and Fall, AEC conducts a national conference for all members. The Annual Meeting & Leadership Conference, typically held in March, focuses on providing leadership, networking and motivational content for extrusion industry executives. The Management Conference, typically held in September, focuses on technical, managerial and marketing information targeted to extrusion industry technical and operational personnel.
AEC Academy - The AEC Academy Online Learning Program is a Learning Management System that provides members with a way to train new and advancing employees, and is intended to supplement members' on-boarding and educational programs. Learners take a quiz after each "module" to demonstrate their understanding of the material.
Business Surveys - AEC members maintain their success - in part - through access to timely data trends. The Council, working through an independent survey research firm to ensure confidentiality, collects data and distributes results to survey participants throughout the year. The surveys are available at no cost to members and survey topics include End Use Shipments, Press Performance Benchmarking, Compensation & Benefits, and Business Trends, a monthly opinion-based snapshot of industry business conditions.

 Benefits of Membership
 Why Become a Member of SMI?
Networking with fellow professionals
Attend SMI’s conventions, conferences, and trade events.  Meet, learn, share problems and successes, form key relationships to enhance your business.
Industry Data that’s not available anywhere else
Only members are invited to participate in confidential industry surveys of quarterly key business trends, safety, wages & benefits, quality, etc.  Results are free to participants!
Power to shape the industry
Through direct involvement you help specify the educational and publications content, resources, meetings, and services delivered to your industry.
Discounts
Receive special pricing as an SMI member through Grainger.
Download the flyer for specific details.
Scholarships
Our annual scholarship program for regular and associate members and their families is available to all full-time employees of SMI member companies. Members click here to apply.
Access to the Springmakers Exchange
SMIHQ.org helps its members as a way to buy or sell excess equipment, inventory, and other products and services for the spring industry with our email newsletter that reaches hundreds of members. To submit information for publication, contact Gabriela Carrasco at gaby@smihq.org or call 847-857-6432.
Access to a staff of professionals
Find professionals to assist you in areas such as regulations, compliance, technical support, and education.  Also at your service, SMI’s team of executive officers and directors is the catalyst behind vital industry programs to promote member interests.
Discounted Products
As a member of SMI, companies receives products at a discount. Available products include Advanced Spring Design Software, Handbook of Spring Design, Encyclopedia of Spring Design and more!  Click here to browse our online store.
Apply Now
To apply for membership, please print and fill out our form here that applies to your company (regular members – springmakers, or associate members – suppliers).

 Any qualified company that meets the membership requirements set forth in AEM’s bylaws is eligible for membership and will be admitted on a non-discriminatory basis.  
AEM is a manufacturer trade association focused on issues specific to manufacturing. Membership is limited to: 
Companies that manufacture equipment, components, or related systems
Service companies that provide solutions to manufacturers
Equipment dealers, distributors, and rental companies are not eligible for AEM membership. However, other industry participants may still engage with AEM through a variety of opportunities, including events, programs, partnerships, exhibiting, sponsorships, and content subscriptions.

 About Us
 CEMA's History
 The story of the Conveyor Equipment Manufacturers Association (CEMA) dates back to 1933, when the idea of an organized, professional association representing the interests of the materials handling and elevating machinery manufacturers was first discussed.
 Industry News
 Goals and Purpose
During its 90-year history, CEMA has grown and developed to respond to the ever-changing environment in which its members do business, while remaining true to its original goals and purposes:
 To promote the common interests of CEMA members and the conveyor industry of the Americas.
 To promote standardization of design, manufacture, and application on a voluntary basis and in such a manner as will not impede the development of conveying equipment and component parts or lessen competition.
 At CEMA’s three in-person and one virtual meeting each year, member companies discuss new developments in conveyor design, technology, and application. Drawing upon the efforts and expertise of our member companies, CEMA provides the conveyor industry with standards, technical publications, safety labels, and safety information.
CEMA works closely with other organizations, such as the Material Handling Industry of America and the Association of Rubber Products Manufacturers, with a shared interest in materials handling, voluntary standards, and business in general. CEMA also maintains contact with government agencies whose activities concern the conveyor equipment industry, keeping a finger on the pulse of federal legislation and regulations affecting the industry, which is then reported to our membership through our Government Affairs Committee.
 Voice of the Conveyor Industry
With an ever broadening membership base and an unwavering commitment to its original puposes, CEMA continues as the voice of the conveyor industry of the Americas, enjoying international prestige and stature throughout the industrial community.

For distributors and manufacturers of any of the spectrum power transmission/motion control (PT/MC) products, PTDA has been the go-to association for more than 60 years.  Membership in PTDA demonstrates your commitment to the PT/MC industry and to working with your channel partners to serve your mutual customers.  Whether you offer just one type of PT/MC product or thousands, your PTDA membership singles you out as an industry leader.  Take a look at who our members are to understand the breadth of our membership. 
PTDA offers four categories of membership with benefits and programs unique to each category.  Learn more about the benefits and criteria for membership by clicking on the links under the member type that best describes your company.
Have other questions about membership? We've got the answers.
Frequently Asked Questions 
Distributors:  A firm, corporation or partnership whose business is involved in the stocking and distribution of power transmission and/or motion control products to original equipment manufacturers and/or end-user markets, and which provides value added services to its customers. Discover the benefits enjoyed by PTDA distributor member companies
 Criteria & PDF Application  Criteria & Online Application
Manufacturers:  A firm, corporation or partnership which manufactures a power transmission/motion control product line, which operates through one or more facilities utilizing its business name located in North America, which has a policy in force of distribution through authorized distributors, and which sells through power transmission/motion control (PT/MC) distributors. Discover the benefits enjoyed by PTDA manufacturer member companies
Criteria & PDF Application  Criteria & Online Application
Associate:  A firm, corporation or individual who provides services directly related to operating a business in the power transmission/motion control (PT/MC) industry and does not meet the criteria of distributor or manufacturer membership. Discover the benefits enjoyed by PTDA associate member companies
Criteria & PDF Application Criteria & Online Application
Educational Institution:  A two- or four-year, post-secondary degree granting educational institution offering courses related to career development in the power transmission/motion control and/or industrial distribution industry. Discover the benefits enjoyed by PTDA educational institution members.

Who Can Be a Member of The FPDA Motion & Control Network?
Distributors
Any corporation, proprietorship, or partnership qualified for membership under these bylaws may be elected a Regular member upon payment of the required fees and dues.
Distributor Application
Manufacturers
Any corporation, proprietorship, or partnership whose business is that of manufacturer of Fluid Power Products (as the Policy Manual defines such products) or whose business is the purchase of fluid power products from a manufacturer to sell under its own brand and uses fluid power distributors as a primary channel to market, and who meets the eligibility requirements adopted from time to time by the Board of Directors may be eligible for Manufacturing Associate membership and may be elected to such membership upon payment of the required fees and dues.
Manufacturer Application
Service/Vendor Associate
Any corporation, proprietorship or partnership that conducts significant business with the fluid power distribution industry, or has shown a significant commitment to the industry, and who meets any eligibility requirements adopted from time to time by the Board of Directors may be eligible for Service/Vendor Associate membership and may be elected to such membership upon payment of the required fees and dues. Service/Vendor Associate members may serve on committees but may not hold elected office.
Service/Vendor Application
Publication Associate
Any corporation, proprietorship, or partnership engaged in the publication of technical journals, textbooks, or trade publications pertaining to the fluid power industry may be elected a Publication Associate Member upon payment of the required fees and dues. (Publication Associate members may serve on committees but may not hold elected office.)

 8/24/26Rods, Fluids, and Seals: The Three Pillars of Leak PreventionIn this Fluid Power Forum episode, host Eric Lanke interviews Trevor Combs, global technical manager for off-highway at Trelleborg Sealing Solutions, about preventing external hydraulic leakage in linear rod applications using a system-level approach emphasized in NFPA’s whitepaper “Preventing Leaks in Fluid Power Systems.”
Combs explains how leakage is driven by interactions among the counter surface (rod substrate, coating, and surface finish), the hydraulic fluid (viscosity index, temperature range, cleanliness/contamination control, lubrication), and the seal system (geometry, materials, and multiple components like primary/secondary seals, wear rings, and wipers). He discusses balancing lubrication film versus leak prevention across extension and retraction strokes, key variables such as pressure, speed, duty cycle, and surface roughness beyond Ra, and innovations including back-pumping seals, pressure-relief buffer seals with integrated check valves, and venting wipers.
Future focus areas include surface treatments, moving away from chrome, PFAS-free materials, compatibility with sustainable fluids, and predictive maintenance using customer data.
Listen Now
 Listen Now
 8/10/2610 Years of the Fluid Power Vehicle Challenge!Host Eric Lanke commemorates the 10-year anniversary of NFPA’s Fluid Power Vehicle Challenge, where university teams simulate, design, build, test, and race hydraulics- and pneumatics-powered vehicles, judged on efficiency, speed/acceleration, regenerative braking, and sustained performance; the program hit a record 32 participating universities.
Guests Dr. Jake Swanson (Minnesota State University, Mankato), Dr. Brian Steward (Iowa State University), and longtime technical liaison Ernie Parker (recently retired from Hennepin Technical College) discuss how the competition’s resources and industry mentoring support student learning, how the challenge has scaled to multiple sites and improved rules over time, and common hurdles such as design, component sizing, ordering and time management, and limited hands-on shop skills. They share memorable competition moments and advise new teams to start early, ask mentors for help, and plan extra time for debugging, emphasizing workforce development and pathways into the fluid power industry.
Listen Now
 Listen Now
 7/27/26Leak Prevention: Protecting Performance, Reliability, and ReputationFluid Power Forum host Eric Lanke interviews Paul Michael, director of the Fluid Power Institute at Milwaukee School of Engineering, about NFPA’s whitepaper “Preventing Leaks in Fluid Power Systems.” Michael shares his background in lubricant formulation and hydraulic testing and describes MSOE’s hands-on fluid power education. The discussion explains why leak prevention is critical to hydraulics because pressurized fluid stresses connectors, hoses, tubes, and seals, affecting reputation and sustainability.
A committee of about 25 contributors developed the report and conducted a voice-of-the-customer survey, with 75% reporting leakage problems tied to customer satisfaction, downtime, and warranty costs. Adapters and connectors were cited as the largest component-related leakage source, with 31 causes identified across design, installation, mounting, selection, and material compatibility. Michael emphasizes application-driven design to minimize maintenance, the importance of standards (including SAE hose and performance tests), and avoiding tapered pipe threads in favor of modern straight-thread and O-ring sealing approaches.
Listen Now
 Listen Now
 7/13/26From Alloy to Application: Engineering Materials for High-Load ApplicationsHost Eric Lanke welcomes Ehren Polheber, corporate fluid power engineer at Scot Forge, to discuss how material science and selection affect hydraulic systems and fluid power component manufacturing. Polheber shares his 22-year fluid power background and 14-year tenure designing and troubleshooting large forging equipment, and explains that correct material grades and heat treatments are critical to avoid catastrophic failures under high loads while enabling lightweight designs in mobile equipment.
He outlines a selection process based on applied loads, operating conditions (fatigue, temperature, corrosion), trade-offs (strength, machinability), and cost of ownership, noting that supplier-customer collaboration is essential. The episode compares casting and forging: castings offer near-net complex shapes at lower cost, while forgings reduce porosity and align grain flow for high-stress, mission-critical hydraulic applications.
Listen Now
 Listen Now
 6/29/26Duty Cycles, Machine Learning, and Energy Efficiency: Optimizing Electrified HydraulicsHost Eric Lanke interviews Barun Acharya, system engineering manager for electrification at Parker Hannifin, about energy efficiency gains from electrified hydraulics and insights tied to NFPA’s white paper and a CONEXPO technology conference. Acharya describes how emissions rules, noise limits, and ESG mandates are driving electrification, and outlines key challenges including unclear duty cycles (addressed via energy mapping), power-density mismatch between hydraulic and electric actuators, complex system integration (CAN, software, EMC, operator feel), and revealed hydraulic noise once diesel is removed.
He explains that traditional inefficiency is largely the engine–pump coupling, while smart hybrid architectures use batteries to buffer transients and run engines near optimal BSFC. He details a hybrid backhoe case with engine downsizing and indoor electric operation, enabled by sensors, data, and machine-learning use for duty-cycle classification, predictive maintenance, and operator coaching.

 Types of Membership
 MHEDA is a thriving material handling business community designed to help you connect with your industry peers and take your business to the next level. Join our growing community of nearly 600 companies and more than 5,000 individuals.
 become a member
 About Our Members
 MHEDA offers a range of membership types designed to serve every segment of the material handling industry. Explore the opportunities and benefits available for your business through MHEDA’s diverse membership options. 
 Industrial Truck 
 A distributor that sells or services material handling vehicles, operated manually, or via internal combustion or electric and includes the related attachments, parts, motive power and maintenance of the vehicle.
 Storage and Handling 
 A distributor that sells, installs or services shelving, racking, and other equipment related to non-automated material handling storage systems, safety and warehouse products.
 Systems Integrators 
 A company that designs, sells, engineers and integrates automated material handling solutions to efficiently move and manage materials within manufacturing or distribution facilities. 
 Manufacturer 
 Any company engaged in designing, producing, and distributing products, equipment, and innovative solutions that meet the needs of material handling distributors & integrators. 
 Supplier 
 Any business that provides products, services, or solutions that support the material handling industry, such as components, technology, or operational resources. 
 Associate 
 Any firm, corporation, partnership, or individual whose expertise and activities align with the MHEDA’s mission and provides specialized services to members.

Join A Committee
 AICC is grateful for the work and support our Committees provide to the Association.
AICC’s Board of Directors needs your help! This is your chance to help lead the association dedicated to advancing the independent industry. All experience levels are welcome to apply.
 Our Committees:
Paperboard, Regulations, & Sheet Supply: focused on external relations & partnerships, government regulations, and paper supply.
Education: responsible for to the oversight of the educational content of all AICC seminars, webinars, and advisory groups.
Conventions: responsible for to the oversight of the content of AICC National Meetings & Summits.
Package Design: help judge package design competitions.
Membership: dedicated to growing the AICC membership & engaging current members.
Marketing: maintaining the AICC brand.
 We want General & Associate Members who:
Believe in AICC
Are strategic thinkers who aren’t afraid to make a meaningful contribution
Have a positive and collaborative attitude.
 What Do You Have to Do:
Show up: committees hold around 4 meetings per year either in person or via conference call.
Be willing to work: committee members will be asked to lead specific actions related to the committee’s purpose.
Do what you say you will do.
 Why You Should Do It:
Significant opportunity for professional development & building relationships
You can help AICC be the Association members need and want
Access up-to-date information about challenges in the industry
You can exchange ideas & perspectives with other volunteer leaders.
We ask all Committee Members to serve for a term of two years. Members who fail to attend three consecutive meetings are considered to be resigned from the committee.

 Eligibility
 To become a General Member, a company must meet the following requirements:
It’s engaged in the corrugated paper converting, folding carton, or rigid box converting business. (A company is in the corrugated converting, folding carton, or rigid box business only it if bears financial and legal responsibility for raw materials, plant, equipment and personnel payroll used in substantial manufacturing activities and is responsible for the quality of the product so produced).
Sells a substantial portion of its product on the open market.
IS NOT a reporting company under the Securities and Exchange Act of 1934 and does not have any shares issued which are publicly traded.
 Dues
 Your Total Annual Sales $50M or Less
Assessed at: $175 per million in sales
Equation: $____ (total annual sales in millions) X $175 = annual dues
Example: A company with $23M in annual sales at all locations 23 X 175 = $4025 (company’s annual dues)
Note: Minimum dues are $1500.
Your Total Annual Sales Over $50M
First $50M Assessed at: 175 per million in salesPLUSSales over $50M assessed at $65 per million
Equation:($____ total annual sales in millions X $170) + ((____ total annual sales in millions) – 50) X 65) = annual dues
Example: A company with $107M in annual sales at all locations (50 X 175) x (57 X 65) = $12,455 (company’s annual dues)
Note: Maximum dues are $25,000.

Corrugated vs Plastic Packaging
As policy-makers, companies and consumers begin to make changes to choose planet over plastics, it’s important to know you can feel good about choosing corrugated packaging.
Corrugated is Sustainable
Corrugated is made from a renewable resource. It is then collected at the end of its life for recycling to begin that process again. Those same fibers get used again to make another box, which leads to a more sustained resource over time.
Industry News
Your go to spot to find all the latest news & announcements on everything corrugated industry and FBA related.
Protects GoodsCorrugated packaging combines structural rigidity with cushioning qualities to protect heavy or fragile contents from damage.
Transports WellCorrugated packaging is lightweight and clean, lowering shipping costs with fewer trucks, less fuel and lower emissions.
Supports Your BrandCorrugated packaging sells your product with high-impact graphics that drive brand awareness and product preference to help close the sale.
RecycledCorrugated packaging is renewably-sourced and roughly 90 percent is recovered and recycled to make new boxes and other paper products.

Thinking Inside the Box: FBA Staff Go Behind the Scenes with Green Bay Packaging
Fibre Box Association (FBA) staff recently traveled to Green Bay, Wisconsin, for a firsthand look at the journey from recovered fiber to finished corrugated packaging with tours at Green Bay Packaging’s Shipping Container Division and Green Bay Paper Mill.
The visit gave FBA staff a deeper appreciation for the equipment, processes, and people involved in turning recovered fiber into new packaging and connected the work we do every day with what happens inside the mill and box plant. The experience reinforced the value of getting out into the field. FBA thanks Green Bay Packaging for the opportunity to tour their facilities, dive deeper into their processes, pick the brains of their staff, and learn more about the industry we serve.

About the Flexible Packaging Association
The Flexible Packaging Association is the voice of the U.S. manufacturers of flexible packaging and their suppliers. The association’s mission is connecting, advancing, and leading the flexible packaging industry. Flexible packaging represents $51.5 billion in direct economic impact in the U.S. and is the second largest and one of the fastest growing segments of the U.S. packaging industry. Flexible packaging is produced from paper, plastic, film, aluminum foil, or any combination of those materials, and includes bags, pouches, labels, liners, wraps, rollstock, and other flexible products.Learn More
