Value of Membership
Helping You Succeed
The Flexible Packaging Association is the leading trade association for one of the fastest-growing segments in the packaging industry. Our members are converters of flexible packaging and suppliers to the industry. FPA provides a wealth of information to its members through focused programs and services.
The Flexible Packaging Association  |  Dues Structure  |  Membership Categories
The Flexible Packaging Association
Membership in FPA is open to manufacturers of flexible packaging (converter members) and manufacturers of material, equipment, or supplies related to the flexible packaging industry (associate members), as well as others (i.e., academic institutions, brand owners, industry vendors, etc.).
Promotes the benefits, contributions, and advantages of flexible packaging through its extensive network, and it advances the industry's products through domestic and international publications and presentations. FPA celebrates the innovation and success of the flexible packaging industry by representing the industry at trade shows and events and by recognizing packaging innovation through its internationally known Flexible Packaging Achievement Awards program.
Provides protection to the flexible packaging industry through an integrated and proactive advocacy campaign that advances the industry through representation to various government and regulatory agencies and employs a coordinated strategic engagement and market outreach program.
Delivers fact-based, business-building, and reliable information and educational forums through the collection, analysis, and publication of its high-quality and timely industry benchmarking financial and economic data.
Improves public understanding of the industry through its continued research and ground-breaking studies. FPA is currently leading an industry effort to better understand all aspects of packaging sustainability, end-of-packaging-life programs, and resource recovery alternatives.
Connects members of the industry through a variety of events throughout the year that focus on educational and networking opportunities, including FPA's Annual Meeting and the FlexForward® Conference.
FPA Dues Structure
CONVERTER, INTERNATIONAL CONVERTER, AND ASSOCIATE MEMBERS
FPA’s annual dues are based on sales in the U.S. of all flexible packaging including converted flexible packaging, plus all materials and equipment sold into the U.S. flexible market and/or industry.
The dues payment is calculated on a formula of $0.45 per thousand dollars of U.S. flexible packaging sales, with minimum dues of $4,500 and a maximum dues of $70,000.
SUPPORTING MEMBERS
FPA annual dues are calculated at $0.35 per $1,000 for U.S. flexible packaging industry-related revenue. The minimum dues are $4,500, and the maximum dues are $50,000.
The banking sector is a subset of this category that will have a flat fee of $50K. Banking is defined as Private Equity, Financial Institutions, and M&A Professionals.
BRAND OWNER COUNCIL MEMBERSHIP
Annual Brand Owner Council membership is a flat $30,000 fee, aligned with the calendar year (January–December).
TRADE PRESS MEMBERS
Trade Press membership is $2,500 per year.
Membership Categories
 Converter
A converter member is categorized by any firm, corporation, or division thereof, engaged in the manufacture and sale within the U.S. of converted forms of paper, film, flexible plastics or foils, or combinations thereof, for sale to the users or distributors of such materials for packaging purposes.
 Join as Converter
 International Converter
International converter members are any firm, corporation, or division thereof, having sales in the U.S. and engaged in manufacture exclusively outside the U.S. of converted forms of paper, film, flexible plastics or foils, or combinations thereof.
 Join as International Converter
 Associate
An associate member is defined by any firm or corporation, or division thereof, engaged in the manufacture within or outside the U.S. and having sales in the U.S. of materials, equipment, or supplies related to the flexible packaging industry.
 Join as Associate
 Supporting
The new Supporting Membership Category is for non-manufacturing companies that support the industry. Supporting Membership will be open to any firm or corporation, or division thereof, engaged in the distribution of materials, equipment, supplies, or flexible packaging, and businesses providing services, within the U.S. and having sales in the U.S. of materials, equipment, supplies or flexible packaging, or services to the flexible packaging industry.
Members in this category are not eligible for a seat on the FPA Board of Directors
 Join as Supporting
 Brand Owner Council
The Brand Owner Council (BOC) is a new membership category within the Flexible Packaging Association (FPA), created to give brand owners a direct voice in shaping the future of flexible packaging. Approved by the FPA Board of Directors in November 2025, the BOC connects brand owners with converters, suppliers, and policymakers to collaborate on the issues that matter most to your business.
Brand Owner Council membership is open to any firm, corporation, or division thereof, engaged in the manufacture and sales of consumer-packaged goods or medical devices and products in the U.S. that utilizeflexible packaging for the containment, distribution, shipping, or storage of those items.
Members in this category will not have voting rights and are not eligible for a seat on the FPA Board of Directors
 Join as Brand Owner Council
 Trade Press
Trade press members are any person, firm, corporation, or division thereof, engaged in the publication of recognized trade magazines related to the flexible packaging industry.
 Join as Trade Press
 Academic
Academic members include universities or colleges with packaging curriculums or departments with activities related to packaging sciences.
 Join as Academic

cPA Membership Benefits
CPA membership is company-based. This means if your company joins the CPA, all individuals within the company are automatically members and can take advantage of our many benefits! Membership Dues are pro-rated throughout the year and are collected on an Annual basis. Renewals are collected within the 4th Quarter of every year.
CPA Regular Membership:
Contract Packagers
Contract Manufacturers
Those who provide 3PL services
Regular Membership Dues pricing is based on your company’s annual revenue in the Contract Packaging sector specifically:
Less than $10 Million Annually: $1,995.00
Between $10 and $50 Million Annually: $2,995.00
Over $50 Million Annually: $3,995.00
Note: Regular members are those who own and/or operate contract manufacturing and packaging facilities. This membership category does not include companies who act as business brokers or intermediaries offering services performed by contract manufacturing packaging organizations. Brokers or intermediaries are allowed to join CPA as associate members.

$3,995 Annually

Note: Service members are those who offer services or products such as packaging materials, labeling and printing, package design, packaging machinery, technology, and testing to other CPA members. Examples of companies who do not fit this definition include private equity and investment firms.

$2,995 Annually

The value proposition will be networking with a broader base, helping shape industry improvements, and connecting with additional industry partners. This group would be asked to help provide a unique perspective and guidance on issues/challenges.
Please Note: Dues will be prorated depending on the time of year your company joins. Full annual dues are collected January 1 of each year. One contact will be listed as Primary Contact, one as Billing Contact, and one as Marketing Contact. Up to 10 additional company members can be added to the company roster.

 Industrial Packaging Alliance of North America
 The Industrial Packaging Alliance of North America represents the interests of manufacturers of new industrial steel drums, plastic drums, fiber drums, and rigid intermediate bulk containers in North America, along with their suppliers. 
 About Us
The Industrial Packaging Alliance of North America represents the leading manufacturers of new industrial steel drums, plastic drums, fiber drums, and rigid intermediate bulk containers in North America. Membership also includes premier suppliers of industrial packaging components, accessories, raw materials, and equipment.
IPANA was formed in 2003 as the result of a partnership between the following trade associations:
 Industrial Steel Drum Institute;
 International Fiber Drum Institute;
 Plastic Drum Institute; and,
 Rigid Intermediate Bulk Container Association.
IPANA constantly promotes the industrial packaging industry’s critical role in the safe and reliable transportation of essential goods around the world. It also represents the industry before U.S. and international regulatory and standards-setting bodies and promotes technological developments that improve product safety, reliability, and sustainability.
The Alliance also serves as a clearinghouse of information. It holds two yearly conferences and numerous webinars that offer members critical information regarding key regulatory and technical issues. These issues can significantly impact a member company’s bottom-line if overlooked. 
 Our Purpose
IPANA’s purpose is to be the leading membership organization for manufacturers of new industrial packaging in North America. To this end, IPANA:
 Effectively represents the industrial packaging industry before U.S. and international regulatory bodies;
 Develops and maintains alliances with other trade associations that represent companies that utilize industrial packaging for the safe transport of their products;
 Promotes the critical role the industrial packaging industry plays in the safe and reliable shipment of essential goods throughout the world;
 Fosters vital technical advances in industrial packaging through research and testing to expand market opportunities;
 Establishes dialogue with allied industries and supply chain partners; and,
 Promotes the use of industrial packaging designed to be safe, reliable, and sustainable throughout its lifecycle while also meeting market requirements for performance and cost. Once used, the packaging is recycled or reconditioned for reuse, reducing its environmental impact and promoting a circular economy.

 Membership
RPA is a membership-based non-profit global trade organization that includes companies participating in the supply, use, and service of a reusable transport packaging system involving products such as pallets, bulk bins, totes, trays, containers, racks, wraps, and dunnage. Regular members are businesses that process or supply raw materials; design, make and market transport packaging products and associated components; provide pooling and logistics services; use and handle the reusable packaging in processing, manufacturing, distribution and retail environments; and offer technology, automation, and handling services to the industry.
Download Membership Brochure
 Membership Categories
 Regular Members
 Companies that design, manufacture and market reusable packaging products; provide pooling or logistics services; provide technology or automation; and supply raw materials for production.
Annual membership dues January – December are based on annual reusable packaging industry sales:
< $10 million:  $3,750
$10 – $100 million:  $7,500
> $100 million:  $15,000
 Primary (End) User Members
 Companies and organizations that use rented or purchased reusable packaging products for the transportation of goods in supply chains (i.e. grower-shippers, consumer products companies, OEMs, retailers, etc.)
Annual dues January – December:  $500.
 Industry Advocates
 Nonprofit associations, government entities or academic institutions who’s work promotes or supports the use of reusable packaging solutions.
No annual dues.
 Reuse Leaders
 Individuals interested in reusable packaging systems or markets in either business-to-business (tertiary packaging) or business-to-consumer (primary packaging) applications, including entrepreneurs, sustainability professionals, consultants, investors, advisors, and packaging engineers.
Annual dues July – June:  $99.
 Qualifications for Regular Company Membership
RPA defines a "reusable packaging product" as having the four characteristics listed below. If your company works with a packaging product that meets these characteristics, your company likely qualifies for RPA membership.
 The reusable packaging product is:
Designed and manufactured for durability and lasting repeatable use in its original or repaired condition over an extended period generally measured in years.
Used in a managed system that ensures its post-use recovery, return and repositioning for continuous purpose.
Intended for packaging source reduction and elimination of single-use or one-way solid waste generation.
Never disposed of or sent to landfill following use, as effort is made to capture the inherent material value for another manufacture or purpose.
It is important to distinguish that a recyclable product or a product made from recycled materials is not necessarily reusable. Reusable products are repeatedly used in their existing form before they are recycled. Products made and intended for a single use destined for recycling are not reusable.
 Company Membership Application
 Qualifications for Individual Reuse Leader Membership
The "Reuse Leaders" membership is open to all individuals interested in reusable packaging systems or markets in either business-to-business (tertiary packaging) or business-to-consumer (primary packaging) applications, including entrepreneurs, sustainability professionals, consultants, investors, advisors, and packaging engineers, for example. RPA offers the individual membership category for practitioners, students, and advocates of reuse systems to engage with companies and experts in the association and to keep informed on industry activities related to reusable packaging, particularly focused on the distribution of goods in the supply chain.
 Individual Membership Application
 Why Join RPA?
For over two decades RPA has been working with member companies to represent and advance the business interests of the reusable transport packaging industry. Today, RPA is the global leader in advocating reusable packaging systems and managing programs for member collaboration on common industry objectives. Join RPA to engage with the reusable packaging industry, network with leading reuse experts and practitioners, build relationships with partners and customers, increase awareness on reuse strategies and tactics, collaborate on industry projects, promote your company and market reuse solutions, and contribute to a growing reuse economy.

EPR influencing manufacturers' packaging decisions
dairy processing
OCT. 6, 2026
The packaging industry’s awareness of extended producer responsibility (EPR) has risen significantly as more states move closer to adoption. Food manufacturers that are impacted by EPR laws will be considering new packaging materials that are more eco-friendly, but they can be more difficult to run through machinery.
“We always hear loud and clear that CPGs (consumer packaged goods companies) are looking for flexibility,” said Rebecca Marquez, director, custom research for PMMI. “They’re looking for modularity. They want something that can be adjusted easily on site that can handle different types of materials.”

Interested in PMMI Membership?
To help us direct you to the proper application type for your company's membership, we ask that you complete the Membership Interest Form.
Membership Interest Form
Membership Categories
Application Process
Booth Space at PACK EXPO
Annual Dues and Fees
Membership Categories
General Membership ($1,750)
Companies that manufacture Processing Machinery and/or Packaging Machinery in North America who:
Are engaged in the manufacturing of processing, packaging or packaging-related converting equipment as defined in Section 3(a) and 3(b) of PMMI's Bylaws.
Have been engaged in the activity in the United States, Canada or Mexico for a period of two years prior to application.
Have minimum annual sales of at least US $500,000 of eligible equipment.
Have applied for membership and for all services and privileges of membership and have been elected by the affirmative vote of the majority of the Board of Directors.
Have agreed to pay all fees, dues and assessments required.
Plant Review For General Membership Applicants
A member of the Membership Committee, PMMI staff, or a selected PMMI member will visit the applicant's plant. The applicant is notified who will conduct the plant review and a timely schedule is arranged. This tour must be complete prior to the vote by The Board of Directors. During the plant visit, the reviewer verifies the information on the application, answers questions about PMMI, discusses PMMI programs and services and encourages the applicant, if accepted, to become fully involved in PMMI. PMMI members feel strongly that the Institute's goals and objectives can be achieved only by an active and participating membership.
As a General Member of PMMI, you receive the following:
Priority booth selection at PACK EXPO trade shows.
Two-tier Exhibit Space discount at PACK EXPO trade shows.
Pavilion Package rates for Exhibit Space in EXPO PACK and PACK EXPO trade shows.
Discounted advertising rates in PMMI Media Group publications and PACK EXPO Show Daily.
Access to the industry's most pertinent statistics and surveys, including the Shipments & Outlook Study and the Packaging Machinery Purchasing Plans Survey.
Access to extensive global market research for international research and networking opportunities with other PMMI members, end users and industry experts. 
Use of the PMMI logo for marketing purposes.
Associate Membership ($2,250)
Processing or Packaging Machinery manufacturers who do NOT manufacture within the United States, Canada or Mexico but have a “presence” who:
Have an International parent/division that is engaged in the manufacturing of processing, packaging and related converting equipment as defined in Section 3(a) and 3(b) of PMMI’s Bylaws.
Have a legal entity incorporated in and a physical presence supplying machinery sales, parts and service in the United States, Canada or Mexico for a period of two years and a minimum of 6 or more employees prior to application.
Invoicing from that location.
Have minimum of at least US$3,000,000 in eligible equipment sales from North American facility.
Have agreed to pay all fees, dues, and assessments required.
Facilities Review For Associate Membership Applicants
A member of the Membership Committee, PMMI staff, or a selected PMMI member will visit the applicant's North American facility. The applicant is notified who will conduct the review and a timely schedule is arranged. This tour must be complete prior to the vote by The Board of Directors. During the visit, the reviewer verifies the information on the application, answers questions about PMMI, discusses PMMI programs and services and encourages the applicant, if accepted, to become fully involved in PMMI. PMMI members feel strongly that the Institute's goals and objectives can be achieved only by an active and participating membership.
As an Associate Member of PMMI, you receive the following:
Priority booth selection at PACK EXPO trade shows.
Exhibit Space discount at PACK EXPO trade shows.
Discounted advertising rates in PMMI Media Group publications and PACK EXPO Show Daily.
Access to manufacturers of processing and packaging machinery solutions.
Networking opportunities with all PMMI members during the Institute's Executive Leadership Conferences, Annual Meetings and other educational programs.
Access to key market research and packaging trends data.
Use of the PMMI logo for marketing purposes.
Component Supplier Membership ($2,250)
Original manufacturers of commercially available processing or packaging machinery components, who are not engaged in manufacturing, packaging machinery or packaging-related converting equipment or processing machinery who:
Have been in business for two years
Have at least $500,000 in component sales per year
As a Components Supplier Member of PMMI, you receive the following:
Priority booth selection at PACK EXPO trade shows.*
Exhibit Space discount at PACK EXPO trade shows.*
Discounted advertising rates in PMMI Media Group publications and PACK EXPO Show Daily.
Access to manufacturers of processing and packaging machinery solutions.
Networking opportunities with all PMMI members during the Institute's Executive Leadership Conferences, Annual Meetings and other educational programs.
Access to key market research and packaging trends data.
Use of the PMMI logo for marketing purposes.
*Companies in China, Taiwan, and Turkey must secure their Trade Show exhibit space through their country’s official broker.
Materials Supplier Membership ($2,250)
Original manufacturers of commercially available packaging materials, containers, resins, polymers, and chemicals, who are not engaged in manufacturing packaging machinery or packaging-related converting equipment or processing machinery who:
Have been in business for two years
Have at least $3 million in materials sales per year
As a Materials Supplier Member of PMMI, you receive the following:
Priority booth selection at PACK EXPO trade shows.*
Exhibit Space discount at PACK EXPO trade shows.*
Discounted advertising rates in PMMI Media Group publications and PACK EXPO Show Daily.
Access to manufacturers of processing and packaging machinery solutions.
Networking opportunities with all PMMI members during the Institute's Executive Leadership Conferences, Annual Meetings and other educational programs.
Access to key market research and packaging trends data.
Use of the PMMI logo for marketing purposes.
*Companies in China, Taiwan, and Turkey must secure their Trade Show exhibit space through their country’s official broker.
Affiliated Supplier Membership ($2,250)
Suppliers to the packaging and processing industry that do not supply components for the build of machinery who:
Have been in the business for two years.
Have at least $500,000 in related sales per year.
Categories may include:
Engineering, Design & Construction Services
Container Engineering & Design
Integrators
New Equipment Distributors
Instrumentation, Automation, Process Control Systems & Software
Material Handling, Distribution & Warehouse Equipment
Product Heating & Steam Equipment
Refrigeration, Cooling, Chilling & Freezing Equipment
Sanitation, Food Safety & Plant Maintenance, Lubricants & Plant Equipment
Transportation, Logistics, Software & Warehouse Service Providers
As an Affiliated Supplier Member of PMMI, you receive the following:
Priority booth selection at PACK EXPO trade shows.*
Exhibit Space discount at PACK EXPO trade shows.*
Discounted advertising rates in PMMI Media Group publications and PACK EXPO Show Daily.
Access to manufacturers of processing and packaging machinery solutions.
Networking opportunities with all PMMI members during the Institute's Executive Leadership Conferences, Annual Meetings and other educational programs.
Access to key market research and packaging trends data.
Use of the PMMI logo for marketing purposes.
*Companies in China, Taiwan, and Turkey must secure their Trade Show exhibit space through their country’s official broker.
The Application ProcessIf your application is complete and your company appears to qualify, you will be granted provisional membership and receive most member benefits beginning in 1-2 weeks. Once granted provisional membership status, you will receive an email with your login information for pmmi.org and a pro-rated invoice. If there are questions with regard to your application, please contact Lindsay Moore, Membership Coordinator, Member Services at lmoore@pmmi.org or 571.612.3184.
For full membership, your application will be reviewed by the Membership Committee prior to a vote by the PMMI Board of Directors. If your application is rejected by the Membership Committee or by the Board of Directors, your dues will be refunded on a pro-rated basis. If approved by the Membership Committee and Board of Directors, you will receive notification of your acceptance and will receive 100% of the benefits available to your membership type.
Regarding Booth Space at PACK EXPOThe PACK EXPO booth space discount will apply to the upcoming show if the membership application is completed and received.*
Otherwise, the booth space discount and priority space selection will begin for the following year’s show. If your membership application is later denied by the Membership Committee or Board of Directors your PACK EXPO space rate will be recalculated at the non-member rate.
*Deadlines apply
Trade Show Priority PolicyPMMI’s member priority program is a method of recognizing member companies that support PMMI shows by offering them priority in initial booth selection. Each PMMI show has its own priority classification.
PMMI will assign the same priority number to a member for a particular show so long as the member continues to exhibit at that show, though adjustments may result from other members being penalized for not exhibiting and from the sale, merger, or consolidation of members.
PMMI members that choose not to exhibit in a particular show will be penalized a designated number of positions as determined by PMMI. The maximum penalty for members at any given time is to remain at the end of the member priority list. Members not exhibiting for three or more consecutive shows will receive the maximum penalty.
Generally speaking, in the event of a sale, merger, or consolidation of a member company, PMMI will agree to reassign the show priority from that company to the surviving entity, provided that the surviving entity remains or becomes a PMMI member.
The member priority program is a loyalty incentive and booth selection mechanism. A priority is not an asset, and members have no property rights in a priority. Priorities may not be sold or transferred. As stated above, reassignment in the event of sale or similar corporate transaction is only by permission of PMMI. PMMI reserves the right to modify or terminate the priority program in its sole discretion.
Visit packexpo.com
Annual Dues and FeesThe Board of Directors sets the dues annually. PMMI invoices members the first of each year.

Meet the Team
Get to know the dedicated leaders guiding PMMI's strategic vision and initiatives.
X
Jim Pittas
President and CEO, PMMI
Jim Pittas leads PMMI as president and CEO, guiding the association’s strategic vision and industry initiatives. Since joining PMMI in 2000 as director of expositions, responsible for the operations and management of PMMI’s number one asset – the PACK EXPO Shows- he has played a pivotal role in expanding the PACK EXPO portfolio, overseeing the launch and growth of multiple shows in the US and Mexico. He also serves on the PMMI Executive Committee and the Board of PMMI’s Education Foundation.
Jim is dedicated to supporting the industry's future through PMMI’s commitment to students and the future workforce. He has been instrumental in growing the PMMI Foundation, which funds scholarships and workforce development initiatives that help cultivate the next generation of packaging and processing professionals. 
Jim is actively involved in MATSO, IAEE, NAM’s Council of Manufacturing Associations, and the Chicago Labor Council. A lifelong Chicago Cubs fan, he enjoys golfing and spending time with his wife and four children.
Jim Pittas
President and CEO, PMMI
View Bio
X
Glen Long
Senior Vice President
As senior vice president, Glen Long plays a key role in advancing the organization’s mission to connect consumer goods companies with packaging and processing suppliers. He focuses on delivering valuable resources that keep members informed of industry developments and equip them with solutions to tackle evolving challenges.
Glen has dedicated his career to the packaging and processing industry. Before joining PMMI’s staff, he was deeply involved as part of several PMMI member companies and served as PMMI chairman and an Executive Committee member from 2004 to 2007. His firsthand experience as a member company leader gives him a unique perspective on the needs of the industry and the value PMMI provides.
Under Glen’s leadership, PMMI has seen significant membership growth, reinforcing its commitment to supporting its members in a constantly evolving marketplace. He is dedicated to providing the tools and insights needed to help companies stay competitive and navigate industry challenges effectively.
Glen Long
Senior Vice President
View Bio
X
David Newcorn
President, PMMI Media Group
David Newcorn brings over 30 years of experience in B2B media within the packaging and processing market to his role at PMMI Media Group. As president, he oversees strategy across advertising, marketing, sales, editorial, and product development, collaborating closely with association and trade show leaders. Throughout his career, David has launched several innovative digital media initiatives, brands, and platforms—including PMMI ProSource, PMMI’s searchable online directory connecting customers with PMMI Member packaging and processing suppliers—demonstrating a commitment to advancing the industry.
David holds a Bachelor of Science from Bentley University.
David Newcorn
President, PMMI Media Group
View Bio
X
Joe Angel
Vice President, Industry Outreach
Joe Angel fosters relationships with education, PMMI members, affiliated organizations, and CPG companies. A founding partner of Summit Media Group, he launched Packaging World magazine in 1994. After Summit was acquired by PMMI in 2014, Joe led PMMI Media Group as president until October 2022 before transitioning to PMMI’s parent organization as executive vice president, industry outreach.
With nearly four decades of experience in packaging, Joe is a strong advocate for packaging education. He serves on the board of the Clemson University Department of Packaging Science, the Packaging Program Council at Michigan State University, and The Dean's Executive Council for Purdue University Northwest’s College of Technology. He is also active with PMMI’s Future Workforce Development Committee.
Joe is a member of the Institute of Packaging Professionals, SIIA’s Connectiv and Association Media & Publishing division, and ANA Business Marketing. He frequently participates in panels and discussions on packaging, processing, and B2B media and continues to contribute to industry thought leadership.
He resides in the Chicago area with his wife, Peggy.
Joe Angel
Vice President, Industry Outreach
View Bio
X
Andrew Dougherty
Vice President, Member Services
Andrew Dougherty is responsible for member engagement, recruiting new member companies, and promoting the association's three pillars: PMMI Business Drivers, PACK EXPO Trade Shows, and the PMMI Media Group. Working in the Trade Association world for more than two decades, Andrew’s strength is helping members leverage PMMI resources to grow their businesses. 
He enjoys visiting member companies to promote PMMI’s products and services and encourage members to take advantage of their company’s PMMI Membership, which includes available resources like Business Intelligence, Workforce Development, Global Marketing, and Industry Services. If your company would like to receive an overview of PMMI and the membership benefits available to every employee, please contact Andrew at adougherty@pmmi.org. 
Andrew Dougherty
Vice President, Member Services
View Bio
X
Tom Egan
Vice President, Industry Services
Tom Egan brings more than two decades of experience in packaging solutions to his work at PMMI, where he has been a key contributor since 2003. He plays an integral role in customer program facilitation, technical services, and industry collaboration. He also serves as a staff liaison to organizations such as the Cold Pressure Council and contributes to meeting content development.
Before PMMI, Tom spent over 20 years in the packaging industry, holding leadership roles at Hoppmann Corporation and Eaton Corporation. He also previously served on PMMI’s Board of Directors and Show Committee, further shaping the association’s strategic initiatives.
With 22 years at PMMI, Tom remains dedicated to advancing industry services, fostering collaboration, and supporting technical innovation.
Tom Egan
Vice President, Industry Services
View Bio
X
Jorge Izquierdo
Vice President, Market Development
Jorge Izquierdo is a mechanical engineer from the National University in Mexico with an MBA from ITAM. He oversees PMMI’s market development, industry, and custom research programs, which aim to strengthen the competitiveness of North American suppliers of packaging and processing technologies. He is also responsible for industry engagement initiatives that promote continuous improvement of processing and packaging operations.
Jorge Izquierdo
Vice President, Market Development
View Bio
X
Craig Silverio
Vice President, Finance
Craig Silverio has dedicated his 34-year career in association management to PMMI, overseeing its financial operations and strategic growth. As vice president of finance, he manages the financial operations of PMMI and its for-profit and not-for-profit subsidiaries, including six managed service association clients.
During his tenure, PMMI has expanded significantly, growing from $6 million in annual revenue to a consolidated $100 million. Career highlights include securing not-for-profit status for PMMI’s general contracting subsidiary, PACK EXPO Services, LLC, and guiding the association through the COVID-19 pandemic, including managing insurance recovery following the cancellation of PACK EXPO International and EXPO PACK México in 2020.
Craig has also played an instrumental role in the success of the PMMI Foundation Golf Tournament, overseeing and supporting the event for nearly 30 years. His leadership and dedication have helped the tournament become a key biannual tradition that supports PMMI’s charitable initiatives and workforce development efforts.
Craig is a member of the American Society of Association Executives and a former chair of the Finance and Administration Roundtable. A graduate of Robert Morris University, he resides in Ashburn, Virginia, with his three children.
A personal highlight of his career was hitting a hole-in-one on the $10,000 hole at an American Society of Association Executives golf tournament in 2006.
Craig Silverio
Vice President, Finance
View Bio
X
Tracy Stout
Vice President, Marketing & Communications
Tracy Stout leads PMMI’s Marketing & Communications department, which is responsible for the promotion of PMMI programs and all communication to members and other industry audiences. Since joining PMMI in 2014, some of the initiatives Tracy has been involved with include the integration of PMMI’s Media Group, specifically the launch of OEM magazine, the OpX Leadership Network rebrand, and the creation and growth of the Packaging & Processing Women’s Leadership Network. 
Under Tracy’s tenure, the Marketing & Communications department launched the association’s first podcast, unPACKed with PMMI, began PMMI’s weekly Conveyor e-newsletter, established an in-house graphic design team and video production capability, and kept pmmi.org up-to-date and reflective of PMMI member needs.
Tracy was born and raised in Northern Virginia and enjoys traveling and spending time with her husband and two daughters.
Tracy Stout
Vice President, Marketing & Communications
View Bio

Laura Thompson
Vice President, Trade Shows
As vice president, trade shows at PMMI, Laura Thompson oversees the management of the PACK EXPO portfolio, including PACK EXPO International, PACK EXPO Las Vegas, PACK EXPO East, PACK EXPO Southeast, EXPO PACK Mexico, and EXPO PACK Guadalajara, as well as PMMI’s contracting business, PACK EXPO Services. She is a graduate of Baylor University in Waco, Texas. 
Laura Thompson

Staff Liaison

Carlos Quintero
Director, Industry Services
Carlos Quintero is Director of Industry Services at PMMI, where he leads the OpX Leadership Network, MaX Member Share Groups, the Industry Relations Committee, and other global initiatives that unite leaders to develop best practices and accelerate results. With over two decades in sales leadership and industry services, he has worked with global manufacturers in track-and-trace, packaging, and processing technologies, delivering strategic solutions that strengthen OEM–end user partnerships. Carlos holds dual degrees in Sociology and Finance from Tulane University and brings a global perspective, sharp business acumen, and a proven ability to drive high-impact industry collaboration.
Carlos Quintero
Director, Industry Services
View Bio
X
Krista DeBrosse
Director, Trade Show Operations
Krista DeBrosse has been with PMMI since 2014, leading the operations team in planning and executing PACK EXPO trade shows across the U.S. She manages everything from vendor relationships and show floor destinations to sponsorships, registration, and PACK gives BACK™. Krista is also actively involved in PMMI’s international trade shows, EXPO PACK Mexico and EXPO PACK Guadalajara, collaborating closely with PMMI’s Mexico office across marketing, sales, and operations.
With over a decade of experience in the exhibitions industry, Krista has helped produce trade shows for audiences exceeding 45,000 attendees and 1.3 million net square feet of exhibit space. Her career highlights include being recognized as one of Trade Show Executive’s Trailblazers of the Year and a recipient of IAEE’s 20 Under 30 award. She is involved in the trade show industry through affiliations with IAEE and currently sits on its Women’s Leadership Committee. Krista also serves as the staff liaison to PMMI’s Emerging Leaders Committee, a network of engaged young professionals in packaging and processing, which is dedicated to advancing the industry through its next generation of leaders via education and networking.
In her spare time, she enjoys being with family and friends, traveling, boating, and reading. 
Krista DeBrosse
Director, Trade Show Operations
View Bio
X
Stephan Girard
Senior Director, Workforce Development
Stephan Girard brings over 29 years of experience in workforce training and development experience to his role at PMMI. As Senior Director of Workforce Development, he oversees efforts to upskill the incumbent workforce and promote packaging and processing industry careers to high school and college students. He is also responsible for the PMMI Foundation, which provides scholarships and financial support for education programs in North America.
Stephan holds a bachelor’s degree from Old Dominion University.
Stephan Girard
Senior Director, Workforce Development
View Bio
X
Kate Torrence
Director, Workforce Development
Kate Torrence leads PMMI’s workforce development initiatives, bridging the gap between education and industry to foster the next generation of manufacturing professionals. She manages relationships with PMMI Education Partners, collaborates with the Future Workforce Committee to enhance student engagement and recruitment, and oversees the PMMI U Skills Fund program.
Kate also plays a key role in expanding the impact of the PMMI Foundation, supporting students, educators, and workforce development programs. Additionally, she leads the PACK Challenge, PMMI’s student STEM competition, which introduces high school teams to real-world packaging and manufacturing challenges, inspiring innovation and hands-on learning.
In her free time, she enjoys staying active and being with her two dogs.
Kate Torrence
Director, Workforce Development
View Bio
X
Rebecca Marquez
Director, PMMI Media Group Custom Research
Rebecca Marquez, a PMMI Business Intelligence team member since 2016, is responsible for PMMI Media Group’s Custom Research initiative, an offering of proprietary research services for PMMI members and packaging industry professionals. In addition to her responsibilities in Custom Research, Rebecca oversees the design, execution, analysis, and production of PMMI’s Business Intelligence market research products for members, internal clients, and the industry.   
With more than a decade of experience in market research, Rebecca has managed and executed research for publicly traded companies and has managed top-tier research vendors both domestically and globally.
Rebecca holds a degree in English Literature from the University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh, bringing a unique blend of analytical and people-focused expertise to her role. As an English Literature major, Rebecca developed a keen ability to analyze complex text, synthesize diverse perspectives, and recognize underlying themes — skills that seamlessly translate into the world of market research. Whether conducting in-depth end-user interviews, competitive benchmarking, or brand perception studies, Rebecca applies the same rigorous attention to detail and interpretive expertise used in literary analysis to decode end-user behavior.
When off the clock, Rebecca enjoys sleeping. But since you can’t do that all day, other hobbies include cooking, traveling, seeing movies at an actual theater, painting/drawing, and anything that will keep her relatively calm.  
Rebecca Marquez

 Membership
 Why Join?
 Home > Why Join?
 Ready to join the leading association for the converters and suppliers of all forms of paperboard packaging?
Membership Types
Request More Information
 Become a member today and receive renowned benchmarking & industry trends, advocacy & regulatory defense efforts, world-class networking & connections, cutting-edge technology & training, and much more. A PPC membership is the premier place for box experts to hone their skills, expand their knowledge, and grow their network.
Sustaining your industry
You are a celebrated member of the paperboard packaging industry—and now it’s time to become a proud member of the premier paperboard packaging industry association. PPC membership sustains your company and your industry. Grow your business with a variety of tools, metrics, and educational programs. Build connections throughout the industry. Contribute to the powerful sustainability story that inspires countless consumers today.
We invite you to become a valued member of PPC. Browse the benefits below to see how we can help your business grow and thrive.
 Here's why
Gain deepIndustry Knowledge 
In addition to timely and relevant articles, white papers, and industry briefs, you’ll have access to RISI’s annual Trends Report, created exclusively for PPC members. This extensive report provides invaluable insight into the folding carton market, both present and future. It’s designed to help executives, sales staff, and marketers identify potential opportunities for growth.
Access member-driven Performance Benchmarks 
Hardworking and focused on their operations, many paperboard packaging manufacturers find it challenging to compare their operational metrics with those of their peers. But PPC membership makes it easy to benchmark and improve.  Members receive access to participate in exclusive benchmarking metrics in the areas of operations, safety, finance, and compensation, helping to remove blind posts and drive performance.
Develop serious Bench Strength 
Your PPC membership doesn’t just apply to you. Your entire team belongs. Here’s your chance to deepen your staff’s knowledge in areas of finance, operations, structural design, and human resources. Through targeted boot camps, seminars, and training, your team will learn what it takes to perform at the highest levels.
Establish a strongNetwork of Peers 
As a PPC member, you’ll be able to build a network of peers and gain access to thought leaders in the industry by attending conferences and workshops. Join one of our working groups in areas like government affairs, marketing and sustainability, and human resources. And remember, your PPC peers are just a phone call away if you find yourself in need of some practical advice.
Grow ourSustainability Story 
The paperboard packaging industry was model of social responsibility before the concept came into vogue. As an industry, we champion environmental stewardship through our sustainable substrate and responsible business practices. We are committed to sharing paperboard’s powerful sustainability story. As growing numbers of consumers begin to factor sustainable packaging into their purchasing decisions, we’ll be there—front and center.
Benefit from Legislative Advocacy 
PPC believes in educating legislators about the importance of paperboard packaging. We regularly coordinate with our members and industry allies like the American Forest & Paper Association to keep advocating at local and national levels. We track legislation impacting our industry at the state level, and we help bring local companies to the Legislature to advocate on behalf of the industry. Together, we can make our presence known.

 Advocating for a Strong Postal System in our Nation's Capital
 by Stephanie Buka, Government Affairs Manager
 Oct 5, 2026
 Photo L to R: Stephanie Buka, government affairs manager, PRINTING United Alliance, Rep. Nikki Budzinski, co-chair Postal Caucus, Ashley Poling, Commissioner, PRC, Holly Lubart, vice president, government relations, News Media Alliance
On September 14-15, PRINTING United Alliance Government Affairs Manager Stephanie Buka traveled to Washington, D.C., on behalf of the industry to participate in several Keep US Posted events supporting key congressional champions of the postal community. Using PrintPAC resources, the Alliance joined industry leaders and stakeholders in recognizing the leadership of Congressional Postal Caucus Co-Chairs Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI) and Rep. Nikki Budzinski (D-IL), as well as Rep. Kweisi Mfume (D-MD), Ranking Member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Subcommittee on Government Operations, which oversees postal issues. These lawmakers have played important roles in advancing policies that support the U.S. Postal Service and the businesses, organizations, and consumers that depend on a reliable and affordable mail system.
The visit also included a happy hour hosted by Keep US Posted Executive Director and former Congressman Kevin Yoder, which brought together congressional staff, postal stakeholders, and industry advocates. The event provided an opportunity to strengthen relationships with key postal policymakers and staff, including members of the Congressional Postal Caucus. Attendees also had the opportunity to engage with Postmaster General David Steiner and Postal Regulatory Commissioner Ashley Poling on issues affecting the future of the mailing and shipping community.
As a mail-intensive industry, printing companies rely on a strong and financially sustainable Postal Service to deliver products, connect businesses with customers, and support commerce throughout the country. Participating in these events helps ensure that the printing industry maintains a voice in policy discussions impacting postal operations, service performance, pricing, and long-term reform efforts.
PrintPAC enables the Alliance to support federal candidates and elected officials who understand the value of the printing, mailing, and graphic communications industry. Through strategic engagement opportunities such as these, the Alliance continues to build relationships with policymakers and advocate for policies that strengthen the industry and the postal network on which so many businesses depend.

 Stephanie Buka
 Government Affairs Manager
 sbuka@printing.org
 Hire This Expert
 Stephanie Buka is the Government Affairs Manager for PRINTING United Alliance. In this role, she supports Ford Bowers, CEO, the Government Affairs team, and coordinates efforts with contracted lobbying firm, ACG Advocacy. Buka is the chief editor of the Industry Advocate newsletter. She is responsible for advocacy campaigns, policy analysis, strategy development and team leadership, all aimed at promoting the Alliance's legislative agenda. She is also responsible for the administration of the Alliance's political action committee, PrintPAC.
Prior to joining the Alliance, Buka served as a senior legislative researcher, and later as a constituent services coordinator, for the 15-member legislative body representing 1.3 million residents of Allegheny County, Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. In addition to drafting legislation and addressing constituent concerns, Buka cultivated strong relationships with appointed and elected officials at the local, state, and federal levels of government.
Buka holds a master’s degree in Public Policy and Management from the University of Pittsburgh, Graduate School of Public and International Affairs (GSPIA). She also earned a master's degree in Criminology from Indiana University of Pennsylvania, along with a Certificate in Forensic Science and Law from Duquesne University.

 ADVOCACY ALERT: Protect Consumer Choice for Paper Communications
 The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) have each issued proposed rules that would shift the delivery of important disclosures from a consumer "opt-in" model to an "opt-out" model for paper communications. While consumers would still be able to request paper copies, these proposals would automatically enroll millions of Americans in electronic delivery unless they take action to choose otherwise.
 Postal Regulatory Commission Denies USPS January Rate Hike Request
 On August 21, the Postal Regulatory Commission (PRC) denied the U.S. Postal Service's (USPS) request for a waiver, concluding that USPS had not demonstrated good cause for deviating from existing rules, had not shown that the proposed change would be consistent with the public interest, and had failed to establish that the request would not unfairly prejudice other participants in the proceeding. The Commission's order cited industry concerns on multiple occasions, underscoring the importance of transparency and adherence to the regulatory framework governing postal rate adjustments.

Welcome to Graphic Media Alliance
Welcome to Graphic Media Alliance (GMA)! GMA is a community of over 250 leading graphic communications companies throughout Ohio, Michigan and northern Kentucky. 
It is our goal to provide programs, offer services and promote an environment that assists you to improve your company’s profitability and adapt to the future. To that end, we have the combination of a terrific staff, excellent programs and the backing of over fifteen affiliated associations across the country including multiple graphic industry groups. We also offer many excellent programs and cost-saving plans to help support your business. GMA is proud to work with many of the most highly regarded technical and management associations in the industry.
We invite you to download our 2026 Calendar of Events and stay informed about this year’s exciting programming. Watch for news on upcoming Executive Leadership Training Series events—designed to support the growth and success of leaders across our industry. 
Thank you for your membership and continued support of Graphic Media Alliance.
2026 ENCORE Leadership Conference
Date: Monday, October 5, 2026Where: Quest Conference Center (9200 Worthington Rd Ste 400, Westerville, OH 43082)Time: 9:00 am - 4:30 pm (Registration and breakfast to begin at 8:00 am)Reception: 4:30 pm - 7:00 pm
Leadership is not just about solving today’s challenges. It is about building the people, systems, strategies, and mindset that prepare your organization for what comes next. ENCORE 2026: Lead Beyond Today brings leaders together for a purposeful journey through the areas that have the greatest impact on success. From building stronger teams and smarter operations to accelerating growth, using data more effectively, and developing yourself as a leader, each session builds on the one before it. You will hear new ideas, learn from experienced leaders, and leave with practical insights you can put to work immediately.
Register Today!
Emerging Leaders Academy
The Emerging Leaders Academy is designed to intentionally prepare the next generation of leaders while supporting today’s senior executives in building continuity, confidence, and long-term organizational strength. Built specifically for the graphic communications industry, this program focuses on practical leadership development that can be applied immediately within your operation.Developed in collaboration with the Center for Great Work Performance, the Academy combines proven leadership frameworks with real-world application. Each session is designed to move beyond theory, equipping participants with the tools, mindset, and structure needed to lead effectively in fast-paced production environments.Delivered through five focused sessions throughout the year, the Emerging Leaders Academy creates a shared leadership language between current and future leaders. Participants will gain clarity in expectations, strengthen communication, and build the confidence needed to lead teams, improve performance, and support long-term organizational growth.
Register Today!
Membership
Networking, education, insurance and buying programs are all common reasons for joining an industry’s association, but like any business decision, becoming a member of Graphic Media Alliance should be evaluated based on each company’s assessment of its potential Return On Investment (ROI) for its dues dollar. Of course, every membership needs to take into consideration intangible beneﬁts including networking opportunities, fellowship with other graphic communications ﬁrms and having a trusted conﬁdant at the Association’s oﬃce to discuss business issues.
Graphic Media Alliance is a trade association, supporting print and graphic communication service providers and their technology partners for over 100 years. GMA offers programs and services to enhance efficiency and profitability in the printing industry, such as workers’ compensation, energy procurement, and discounted credit card processing, to name a few. Graphic Media Alliance is part of the Americas Printing Association Network (APAN), representing more than 5,000 industry members working with 13 industry associations to actively provide the most accurate and up-to-date technical, environmental, and business-related services available in the graphic/printing industries.
Join Today!
At a Glance
Graphic Media Alliance (GMA) is a forward-thinking association that supports the graphic communications industry in Ohio, Michigan, and Northern Kentucky. By becoming a member of GMA, your organization can benefit from various programs and services that help enhance efficiency and profitability in the printing industry. Some of the key benefits include:
Advocacy: GMA represents its members’ interests at the local, state, and national levels by addressing legislative issues and ensuring compliance with various regulatory bodies. GMA also provides training and education to help members stay up-to-date with the latest trends and technologies in the printing/graphic communications industry.
Workforce Development: GMA has developed a 3-year strategic plan that includes building relationships with educational institutions and educators in all four regions and developing workforce pipelines for members and associate members. GMA’s workforce development efforts have resulted in an increase in student participation in various events.
Networking: GMA provides various opportunities for members to network with peers, industry experts, and potential customers. Monthly regional gatherings, advisory council meetings, print week events, and leadership conferences are some of the networking opportunities that members can take advantage of.
Services for Success: GMA offers over 30+ programs and services to its members, most of which can generate a positive ROI on membership by utilizing 2-3 programs.
Scholarship Fund: GMA’s Printing Industries Education Funds (PIEF) annually funds 10-15 students, awarding $2500 scholarships, which are renewable for up to 4 years. Over the last ten years, PIEF has paid over $230,000 in scholarships as an investment into the future workforce.
By joining Graphic Media Alliance, your organization will not only enhance its profitability but also support the printing industry’s workforce development initiatives, advocacy efforts, and scholarship programs. GMA’s commitment to innovation and development ensures that it will remain a vital resource for the graphic communications industry in Ohio, Michigan, and Northern Kentucky for years to come.
Andrew L. Schall, PresidentGraphic Media Alliance
GMAENERGY(+)
GMAENERGY(+). As an Association committed to driving efficiency and cost-effectiveness, we're proud to expand our energy savings program to encompass a broader spectrum, now including gas, electric, demand response, and green energy solutions. While our legacy services have consistently aimed at minimizing operational expenses, our new program takes it a step further by introducing tailored solutions in each region we serve. Moreover, it's not just about cost reduction; in numerous instances, this program opens doors to revenue-generating opportunities.
We understand that staying ahead in an ever-evolving landscape requires innovation and adaptability. GMAENERGY(+) embodies this ethos by offering diverse and region-specific solutions to empower your business. We're dedicated to providing avenues for new streams of revenue.
Embrace the possibilities that our program brings, and let's navigate this landscape together toward a more sustainable and prosperous future.
Request More Information
Experience Print: Imagine A World Without Print
Graphic Media Alliance is delighted to share ExperiencePrint.org, a new campaign to promote the graphic communications and printing industry to students and young adults as part of the organization's workforce development strategy. ExperiencePrint.org provides experiential learning opportunities, hands-on experiences, connections with GMA member companies, site tours, career opportunities, and credentialing to encourage the next generation to explore and immerse themselves in the dynamic field.
This initiative is part of GMA's commitment to developing the next generation of talent and leaders in the printing and graphic arts industry. ExperiencePrint.org will serve as a platform for students and young adults to learn about career opportunities available in the industry and to interact with industry professionals.
The campaign features an initial promotional video titled "A World Without Print," highlighting the presence of print in our daily lives. The video showcases imagery of touchpoints with print and scenes from life outside of school. The initiative aims to ignite passion for the graphic communications and printing industry by providing young people hands-on experiences and connecting them with industry professionals.
Graphic Media Alliance encourages businesses and individuals to join them in creating a bright future for the industry. For more information and to get involved, visit ExperiencePrint.org today!
GMA Newsline
Help Us Share Your Story!
Graphic Media Alliance is proud to launch GMA Member Newsline, a simple and effective way for you to share company updates, milestones, community outreach, innovations, or industry insights directly with our team. Whether it’s a facility expansion, new hires, awards, retirements, or charitable initiatives—your story matters.By submitting your company’s news, you ensure timely visibility and recognition within our growing community. It only takes a few minutes, and your submission may be featured in The Communicator, on our website, or in future member spotlights! Click the logo below to access our online form. 
Share Story

Membership
The National Wood Flooring Association (NWFA) is an international not-for-profit trade association representing all segments of the hardwood flooring industry, including manufacturers, distributors, retailers, installers, importers/exporters, inspectors and consultants.
Join
Renew
As such, NWFA’s mission is to unify and strengthen the wood flooring community through technical standards, education, networking, and advocacy.
We accomplish this through various programs and services, such as hands-on and online training, our annual Wood Flooring Expo, Hardwood Floors magazine, and technical standards and publications that are recognized worldwide.
Learn more about the NWFA and our available programs and services in our Marketing Toolkit.
All NWFA members agree to abide by the association’s bylaws and standards of professional conduct upon joining:
To deal with customers with honesty and integrity.
To promote the merits of products and services without degrading competitors.
To reveal all the material facts so that the truth about products and services may be understood fully.
To abide by all governmental regulations and statutes.
To support the NWFA and its goals and purposes toward advancing the wood flooring industry.
To commit no act that would discredit profession or the wood flooring industry.
To abide by these Standards of Professional Conduct and recognize the NWFA as the authority in all matters relating to interpretation and enforcement of these Standards, within prevailing legal limits.
Join NWFA
Become a member of the NWFA and unite with wood flooring professionals from across the globe who are dedicated to education, industry standards, and quality service and products. Membership dues are $599-$699 (depending on business type) and are paid annually. To get started, click here.  
Renew Membership
NWFA membership runs from July 1 through June 30 each year. Membership dues are $599-$699 (depending on business type) and are paid annually. Renew your membership before July 1 to maintain access to all of the valuable resources the NWFA has to offer. Renew today.
MEMBERSHIP BENEFITS
Get connected and get involved. The NWFA offers a variety of programs and opportunities to help you grow your business. From nationally recognized technical standards, to savings programs on services you use regularly, and everything in between, we’ve got you covered.
Member Type
The NWFA represents all segments of the wood flooring industry. Learn more about each member type and the specific services we have to offer for each.
Giving Back
The NWFA has established multiple relationships with charitable organizations. This gives you the opportunity to use your talents to give back to those in need, while promoting the benefits and uses of wood flooring. Check out the ways you can get involved and start giving back!
Member Recognition
Each year, NWFA celebrates craftsmanship, and the people behind it, on a national and international level. There are multiple opportunities to recognize your work, from Wood Floor of the Year awards to “40 Under 40” recognition, there are plenty of achievements to help set you apart.

 Who we are
Founded in 1921, the Decorative Hardwoods Association, formerly known as Hardwood Plywood and Veneer Association, represents the hardwood plywood, hardwood veneer, and engineered hardwood flooring industries. Together we produce 90% of the hardwood plywood stock panels and hardwood veneer manufactured in North America.
Our passion and mission are to educate and provide the resources that will help you make informed decisions when it comes to choosing the best and highest quality products we have to offer. For us, the authenticity, the beauty of real wood, and our pride in craftsmanship are what we stand for and behind.
What we stand for
How do you measure the authenticity of real wood? How do you evaluate passion and pride? For us, it’s about holding ourselves to a higher standard – yours. It’s a legacy that’s been handed down from one generation to the next for over 95 years. Is that something to be proud of? You bet it is. And it’s that kind of pride in quality craftsmanship you can see and expect in everything we do.

WCMA Manufacturer Membership Dues Explained
The basis of assessing membership dues in the WCMA, as approved by the Board of Directors and ratified by the membership, is as follows:
Dues shall be computed at a rate of $1.00 per $1,000 of annual dimension and wood component shipments. Canadian members convert their Canadian dollar shipments to US dollars and pay in US dollars to equalize the exchange rate difference.
For annual shipments below $1,000,000, minimum dues shall be $1,000 per year.
For annual shipments above $3,000,000, maximum dues shall be $3,000 per year.
Members may choose to pay their dues in monthly or quarterly installments.
The following classifications are to be used to determine the kind of products on which dues are paid.
Wood Dimension & Component Parts, including rough or surfaced flat stock, solid, glued up or engineered dimension and components parts, as set forth in WCMA’s Rules and Specifications for Dimension and Woodwork. This includes all types of rough, semi-machined and completely machined wood component products, glued or not glued, constituting furniture, cabinets and related decorative/specialty wood products.  
Interior Trim and Mouldings: interior trim, mouldings and millwork of standard or special work.
Stair Treads and Risers: stair treads, risers, thresholds and other staircase parts worked to standard or special specifications.
Contributions to the Wood Component Manufacturers Association are not deductible as charitable contributions for federal income tax purposes. However, dues payments are deductible by members as an ordinary and necessary business expense. WCMA estimates that the nondeductible portion of your dues which are allocable to lobbying is less than the minimum making your total dues deductible as an ordinary and necessary business expense.

General Membership
Any firm or individual whose primary business is the manufacturing of wood or composite cabinets and related wood or composite products for government, industrial, commercial or residential applications is eligible for Active Membership.
Annual dues for new or renewing members are $425. Or try our monthly subscription for $50/month.
Join Now
DON'T TAKE OUR WORD FOR IT
Read testimonials from current members to learn why they belong to the CMA.
A CMA membership offers the following opportunities:
Networking & Education
We realize that connecting with other members, learning from others, is what the CMA is all about. Because of that premise, we typically hold several regional events throughout the year, as well as provide opportunities to meet other members at the industry's major trade shows, such as plant tours, educational seminars, and webinars. Learn more
ProCoach Mentoring
ProCoach offer members one-on-one communication to receive insights into problems they may be experiencing in their business. We pair them with a compatible member who has been there, done that, and succeeded. The goal of the program is to engage new and existing CMA members through personal interaction, and this often leads to long-lasting friendships.
Wood Diamond Awards
The Wood Diamond Awards program is in an exceptional way to have the finest examples of your work generate advertising that actually produces results. Professional news releases prepared and distributed by the CMA not only increase your online presence and site ranking, but can also get you featured in industry publications seen by thousands of your potential clients. Buying advertising in these publications is expensive and can yield a poor return on investment. However, being featured can result in an entirely different outcome.
Shop Finder
Access to the Shop Finder can help you find a local member where you can leverage your excess capacity to generate additional work or using their capabilities to benefit your business. A major advantage of membership is cooperative nature of its members.
Discussion Forums
Exclusive peer to peer networking online in our discussion forums. This is extraordinary access to the accumulated knowledge and experience of hundreds of woodworking business owners. Have a problem? Need a second opinion? Or how about needing some CNC programming assistance on a weekend with a deadline looming? You don’t need to reinvent the wheel. Someone else already has and is willing to give you the answers and short cuts they found.
PROfiles Magazine
The official magazine of the CMA, this quarterly publication is where members are featured along with industry news and relevant content for today's professional woodworker. Read our online archives.
Monthly E-Newsletter
A key aspect to keeping your business current and attractive to more clients is maintaining an understanding of changing design and industry trends. Trying to play catch up with a changing market is much more expensive and time consuming than staying relevant. The newsletter keeps you up to date with CMA events and activities, educational offerings, industry news and more.
Leadership Opportunities
The CMA's Board of Directors is always looking for a few good men and women to serve the industry and help grow the association. The election term is three years, starting in July, while nominations occur in the Spring. Learn more about what board service involves.

Who We Are
The International Wood Products Association is the leading international trade association for the North American international wood products industry. We bring together every segment of the global supply chain, from producers and service providers to importers, distributors, manufacturers, and retailers.
Our Mission
IWPA serves as the trusted global resource for professionals, policymakers, and users of forest products by: (1) Advancing policies to support sustainable forest stewardship (2) Developing education to nurture industry knowledge and expertise and (3) Cultivating a community to promote forest resources and employment
Become a Member Today
Join our community and grow with us. IWPA represents companies and organizations worldwide. We create value for our members by uniting businesses, providing them with opportunities for improvement and growth, and representing them with a powerful voice.

Membership with IWPA
Become part of a growing network of businesses dedicated to the imported wood products industry.
GET IN TOUCH
Why Join?
Support Your Business with Industry Insight, Advocacy, and Community
International Wood Products Association enjoys the membership and support of hundreds of businesses involved in the global wood products trade. 
From suppliers to importers, distributors, manufacturers, and retailers, IWPA offers critical information and services that help support their business. Service providers (insurers, ports, customs brokers, law firms, certification bodies) also gain valuable industry information and connection from IWPA membership. 
Through IWPA membership, Voting, Associate and Overseas Members gain access to the community of fellow members, a voice in Washington, D.C. and many programs, services and products specifically tailored to our industry.
A partnership between a strong wood products industry and sustainable forests are the best solution to secure a healthy future. IWPA provides the timely information and tools you require to ensure a bright tomorrow.
Members of the International Wood Products Association include companies and organizations worldwide which are involved in the many activities required to produce and import a wood product into the United States. 
VIEW MEMBERSHIP CATEGORIES
What Your Dues Support
Your dues power the advocacy, market insights, and programs that support the wood products industry.
Protect Your Ability to Conduct Business
IWPA helps keep the U.S. market open for globally sourced wood products through legislative and regulatory advocacy. IWPA is your staff in Washington, D.C. fighting for your business. In addition to advocacy, IWPA staff works with contacts at federal agencies to help prevent costly permit and port delays.
Education
IWPA has been a leader in the development and offering of wood trade compliance training. From our in-person classes to online training to World of Wood Convention sessions, to our weekly newsletter and webinars, IWPA provides a host of opportunities for staying abreast of the ever-changing regulatory landscape and compliance requirements.
Grow Your Business
IWPA exists to help expand the market for globally sourced wood products. We help companies stay competitive in a rapidly changing trade environment by providing critical information, along with networking, promoting the use of legally sourced international woods, marketing tools, and advocacy designed to help your business flourish and grow.
VIEW OUR MOST RECENT ANNUAL REPORT
Explore Membership Categories
Membership is on a calendar-year cycle (January to December). Dues will be pro-rated the first year for new members who join after March 31.
Voting Members
Voting Members are companies located in North America that are actively engaged in the sale of imported wood products in the U.S., whether for their own account, as commissioned agents, or other similar sales capacity.
You should join IWPA as a Voting member if you are:
U.S. importers
Paneling processors
Manufacturers
Sales representatives
Wholesalers
Retailers
Distributors
Commissioned Agents
Associate Members
Associate Members are companies and individuals, located in North America or worldwide, with interests allied to the industry, such as suppliers of services to the imported wood products industry.
You should join IWPA as an Associate member if you are:
Transportation companies
Customs brokers
Port authorities
Warehouse terminal operators
Custom kiln dryers
Insurance brokers
Consultant
Software providers
Law firms

Overseas Members
Overseas Members are companies or organizations not based in North America which manufacture and/or export wood products to the United States, including both companies involved in the industry or those who provide services related to the industry.
Subsidiary Members
Subsidiary Members are companies that fall under the control of a Voting, Overseas, or Associate member. The companies must be controlled by the member company and not simply a supplier. If the controlling company is a Voting Member, the Voting Member must include the Subsidiary Member’s annual sales in their sales volume declaration. 
Association/Trade Organization
Associations or trade organizations whose members are involved in the trade, manufacture, or use of international woods are welcome to join IWPA. In addition to member benefits conveying to the organization's employees, some benefits can be conveyed to the organization's members, thereby increasing the benefits you offer to your membership.

 Get Started With Your Membership
 The American Home Furnishings Alliance is committed to promoting the growth and global leadership of our member companies by providing exceptional advocacy, promoting effective standards, advancing meaningful environmental programs, offering relevant training and development opportunities and serving as the preeminent media resource on business and produce trends in home furnishings.
 Alliances are based on common interests. Regardless of where their products are sourced, AHFA member companies share an interest in:
 Unity
 Promoting industry unity through powerful partnerships capable of impacting consumers and influencing the outcome of important industry issues.
 Access
 Gaining access to valuable resources and money-saving services that give their companies a competitive advantage in our rapidly changing industry.
 Influence
 Supporting a strong watchdog organization with influence over regulations and standards that impact the day-to-day operations of member companies.

 AHFA Membership Application
The American Home Furnishings Alliance is a nonprofit trade association incorporated in North Carolina. AHFA's bylaws require your company to be a manufacturer or importer of home furnishings products for wholesale distribution in the United States. Any non-confidential information required to assist in the approval of this application must be provided. Government agencies do not qualify for membership.
Upon membership acceptance, you agree to support and promote the affairs and activities of the American Home Furnishings Alliance and will receive all the rights and privileges of membership.
All memberships are renewed January 1 of each year. In the event of cancellation, dues cannot be refunded. If joining after the beginning of AHFA's fiscal year, the full dues amount paid will be prorated and applied to the subsequent fiscal year. Dues amounts are recalculated annually, based on the sales for the previous calendar year ending December 31. Members will be billed the first working day of January, the first day of the AHFA's fiscal year.

Become a Member of The Association of Woodworking & Furnishings Suppliers® 
The Association of Woodworking & Furnishings Suppliers® (AWFS®) is the largest national trade association in the U.S. representing the interests of the broad array of companies that supply the home and commercial furnishings industry.
Membership Application
Any proprietorship, partnership or corporation which supplies products to the woodworking and furnishings manufacturing industry, and whose principal business is not woodworking or furnishings manufacturing, and which is interested in promoting the objectives of this Association, is eligible for regular membership.
Regular Membership Application
Benefits of AWFS® Membership
If you are an exhibitor at the AWFS®Fair, membership in AWFS® will earn you a discount off the exhibit booth cost (see chart on membership application).  If a member, all of the College of Woodworking Knowledge™ (CWWK™) seminars at the Fair will be discounted. Through educational seminars, association publications, up-to-the minute information affecting our industry, AWFS® helps to keep you run your business more effectively.
Click here to read about our member benefits
Society of Wood Manufacturing (SWM)
Membership is open to all individuals working for AWFS® member companies. AWFS® member companies get three (3) complimentary SWM memberships and a special reduced rate of $25 for each additional member. Activities include: fund raising, educational, and networking events in Southern California.
