 Member FAQs
 Home » Member Programs » Member FAQs
 How do I renew my IDA membership? 
 IDA membership runs annually from January 1 through December 31. The company administrator (a designated role or the default role for companies with only one point of contact) for active IDA members can login and renew online here. You can also renew by mailing a check for your annual membership dues to the address below. Please contact [email protected] with any questions.
 How do I join IDA? 
 You can find more information about joining IDA here.
 I am having trouble logging into my account, what can I do? 
 Click here for instructions to log into your existing account or create a new one.
 I want to get accredited or sign up my technicians for training. Who should I contact? 
 Training and accreditation is provided through the Institute of Door Dealer Education and Accreditation (IDEA). IDEA is a private, independent organization which provides educational resources, training systems and professional development programs for companies engaged in the sale, installation and service of door and access systems products. These programs include Door Dealer Accreditation, Residential Installer Certification, Rolling Steel Fire Door Technician Certification and Commercial Sectional Door Systems Technician Certification. You can find more information here.
 Where can I view the digital version of the IDA Magazine? 
 You can find more information about IDA Magazine and view the current issue here.
 I would like to be a sponsor or exhibitor at an upcoming IDA event, who should I contact? 
 Information about upcoming IDA events can be found here. 
 Still have unanswered questions, contact us.

 Membership

 Our member community is 1,900+ companies strong and represents all aspects of the glazing and glass building products industry. We are contract glaziers. We are full-service glass companies.  Business Benefits

 Membership Benefits
 Serving the Industry
Education, technical publications, industry news and trends, events.
 Our Resource Hub
Who Should Join?
Companies of any size, who identify as:
Glazing Contractors
Full-Service Glass Companies
Specialty Residential Window and Door Companies
Fabricators of Glass, Metals or Components
Fabricators/Manufacturers of Completed Glass Products and Systems
Primary Glass Manufacturers
Suppliers of Hardware, Machinery/Equipment, Tools/Supplies and other Glass-related Products
Service Providers (Software/Systems/Testing/Finance)
Manufacturers' Reps
Architects, Engineers, Consultants
 Our tools, resources and community will help save you time, save you money and make your business better. NGA recognizes the value that your company brings to the glass and glazing industry, and we want you as a member!
 Membership Dues
 Regular members are companies who are actively engaged in the manufacture, sale, installation, distribution, fabrication, replacement or repair of glass and glazing industry products. Affiliate members are companies who have a professional interest in the glass and glazing industry such as architects, engineers and consultants.
 Expand All / 
 Collapse All
 Regular Member
 Membership is company based. Dues are based on your company's global gross annual sales in glass and glass-related products. Members are required to pay the highest dues for which they qualify.
Annual dues based on your company’s gross annual sales, per the chart below.
Annual Sales – Annual Dues
Under $1 million - $395
$1-2 million - $695
$2-3 million - $1,015 
$3-5 million - $1,365
$5-10 million - $1,855
$10-20 million - $2,765
$20-50 million - $3,845
$50-100 million- $6,160
$100-500 million - $9,830
$500 million+ - $11,615
Member companies can add additional or subsidiary locations to their membership to receive the same NGA benefits, but should factor each location's revenue in to their Annual Sales amount. Please contact membership@glass.org or 703-442-4890, ext. 127 for assistance.
 Affiliate Member
 Membership is company based. Consultants, architects and engineers are considered Affiliate members and have a flat annual dues rate.
Annual dues - $530

A Unified Voice for a Thriving Glass Industry
GMIC connects, supports, and inspires the world’s leading glass producers, suppliers, and researchers.We serve our members through government and trade advocacy, the promotion of glass usage, the coordination of technical initiatives, education and training, workforce development, and the facilitation of new ways to meet sustainability demands. We do for you what you can’t do alone.
Mission
The mission of GMIC is to facilitate, organize, and promote the interests, economic growth, and sustainability of the glass industry through education and cooperation in the areas of technology, productivity, innovation, and the environment.
LEARN MORE
GMIC members include glass melting companies, glass product suppliers (material, equipment, technology, and services), laboratories, colleges and universities, glass users, industry consultants, and individuals. We connect all segments of glass manufacturing including container, flat, fiber, and specialty.
Member List
In addition to the support of a proactive national trade association, GMIC members receive industry communications, conference fee discounts, courses and symposia, supplier and customer referrals, and much more.

 Advocacy & Technical Resources
 Advocacy & Technical Resources
 NGA promotes and defends the use of glass in the built environment; our advocacy and technical initiatives respond to the current challenges to our industry. We thank our volunteer members, industry partners and expert consultants who work to ensure glass and glazing is at the forefront of all discussions impacting building regulations and innovation in construction. 
We are:
working with domestic and international standards and codes bodies
providing education on the benefits of glazing and glass building products
representing the glass industry’s best interests on key issues
 School Security: NGA's 2025 Top Advocacy Priority
 Image
NGA advocates for school security glazing system requirements in State and Federal legislation. Learn about the key issues and next steps to include security glazing in building codes. Download our School Security one-pager, Windows and Doors Respond First.
Advancing School Security Standards: School Security Workshop
During NGA Glass Conference: Carlsbad, the NGA School Security Task Group and industry experts addressed the importance of developing standardized security measures for fenestration systems. Testing methods, such as ASTM F3561 for forced-entry resistance, emphasize the need for industry-wide clarity on terms like “bullet-resistant” rather than misleading claims of “bulletproof” glass. The workshop helped attendees to better understand the role of surface-applied films in enhancing security, and how the absence of clear codes and standards for school security remains a challenge, underscoring the need for coordinated efforts in upcoming building code proposals. For more on this topic, watch our on-demand Thirsty Thursday webinar. 
Standard for Forced-Entry Resistance of Glazing Products 
NGA announced at the NGA Glass Conference: Chicago a new ASTM International document created through the F12 Security Committee and NGA’S School Security Task Group, entitled Standard Test Method for Forced-Entry-Resistance of Fenestration Systems After Simulated Active Shooter Attack. Download: ASTM F3561 Standard Test Method for Forced-Entry-Resistance of Fenestration Systems After Simulated Active Shooter Attack

 Membership Dues
 Regular members are companies who are actively engaged in the manufacture, sale, installation, distribution, fabrication, replacement or repair of glass and glazing industry products. Affiliate members are companies who have a professional interest in the glass and glazing industry such as architects, engineers and consultants.

 International Window Film Association
 The IWFA is the world’s definitivesource of window film information.
 IWFA AT A GLANCE
 The International Window Film Association is a Nonprofit Trade Association that provides unbiased educational information about Window Film and its many benefits. We are a unified industry body of window film dealers, distributors, and manufacturers that facilitates the growth of the window film industry by providing research, influencing policy, and promoting awareness of window film.
 RESIDENTIAL 
 Residential consumers will find the answer to many common complaints by installing window film. These films can help reduce fading of furnishings, minimize hot or cold spots, and help eliminate glare causing viewing issues with home electronics.
 Learn More
 COMMERCIAL 
 The main benefits for commercial building owners and managers are solar heat control for cost savings, occupant comfort, fade protection, glare control, and exterior building aesthetic improvement. The cost of a window film installation is often justified and budgeted based on the payback in energy savings.
 Learn More
 AUTOMOTIVE 
 Automotive window films offer many benefits similar to window films applied on windows, doors and skylights. Window films block up to 99% of the sun’s harmful UV rays that may lead to skin damage and fading of car interiors. Window films can reduce the amount of heat coming into the interior and reduce glare as well.
 Learn More
 Benefits Of Window Film 
 Window Films have different characteristics that can help with issues from comfort to UV protection. Explore the wide range of benefits quality installed films can achieve for you.

 Get to Know the IWFA
 The International Window Film Association is the only non-profit organization specifically for the advancement and education for Window Films. The organization has served the industry over its 30+ year tenure as the most trusted source for information pertaining to Window Film and its many benefits.
 The European Window Film Association 
 The European Window Film Association serves as a chapter of the IWFA operation in continental Europe.
The EWFA promotes relationships with other like-minded organizations and maintains close contact with stakeholders and decision-makers in Europe, whether in Brussels or at national and local levels. Their objectives are to continue to reach and influence a wider audience, increasing the awareness of what and how window film can improve the environment and how people work and live around windows

Better Products. Better Policy. Better Decision-Making. For All of Us.
WDMA’s membership includes manufacturers of windows, exterior doors and skylights; architectural door manufacturers; suppliers to the industry; and professionals including specifiers, builders, contractors and architects across United States and Canada.
Through our member structure we provide a full team of advocacy professionals to influence and drive policy and reduce unnecessary regulatory burdens across the window, door and skylight industry.
WDMA works closely with leading industry organizations, including ICC, ANSI, AIA, and the ENERGY STAR program to ensure we are fully aligned to the current and future needs of the industry.
Making sure members’ views are represented is what makes WDMA unique. By representing members and their requirements, we remain at the heart of the window, door and skylight community.Learn more about why WDMA is home to the following:
For Manufacturers of Windows, Skylights and Exterior Doors
For Architectural Door Manufacturers
For Component Material and Service & Machinery Suppliers
Why WDMA?
As the window, door and skylight industry landscape becomes more complex and unfair trade practices increasingly threaten the industry, WDMA is your voice in Washington, DC.
Throughout its 90-year history, WDMA has proven to be an organization that is focused on moving the industry forward. Our programming for members, their employees and its leadership in building, energy efficiency and life safety codes; energy and environmental regulations; green building standards; emerging trends and technology; operation and manufacturing planning; advancements in logistics, equipment and material handling; and certification and quality assurance provide members with a tremendous value proposition.
WDMA meetings give members the opportunity to learn from some of the best in the industry.
As a member, you can participate in the exchange of ideas that will define the technical standards and regulations needed to meet the future demands of a fast-changing industry, and drive research that increases confidence and demand for higher performance products through our Committees.
Gain unequaled access to leading edge information and insight related to product trends, features and value. WDMA members have access to unique data reports that serve as an essential tool for strategic business planning, including monthly summaries of housing conditions and economic indicators.
Discounted conference registrations, online purchases, and advertising opportunities allow for members to network and gain exposure through direct contact with industry vendors and consumers.
WDMA is the only association that enables industry professionals to partner with key influential executives from the most innovative window, door, and skylight manufacturers in North America.

Introduction
Membership in this organization shall be limited to North American based persons, corporations, or partnerships engaged in the pre-formed flexible sheet membrane roofing industry. Membership shall not include any of the above whose primary business is installation.
REGULAR voting membership in this organization shall be limited to persons, corporations, or partnerships which manufacture or market flexible sheet membrane roofing systems; but not including independent manufacturers’ representatives or distributors.
Associate voting membership in this organization shall be limited to persons, partnerships, corporations and other forms of business entities that manufacture and/or market raw materials, components, accessories, tools or equipment used in or for the flexible sheet membrane roof systems industry.
Affiliate Membership. Affiliate membership shall be limited to persons, partnerships, corporations, and other business entities whose primary business is professional roof consulting (such as IIBEC members with RRC certification), roofing industry architects (such as AIA members), those who specify (such as CSI members with CDT certification), independent testing professionals and other entities (such as those ISO 17025-accredited by IAS), and other professional and accredited consultants in and for the flexible sheet membrane roof systems industry.
We agree to abide by the Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws of SPRI, to pay all levied dues and assessments, and to offer our cooperation in the activities of SPRI to further its objectives consistent with SPRI’s Bylaws, policies and requirements.

What is single-ply roofing?
Single-ply membranes are any flexible sheets of compounded synthetic materials that are manufactured in a factory to strict quality control requirements.Single-ply roof systems provide the greatest strength, flexibility, and long-lasting durability for your home or commercial building.
 What is SPRI?
SPRI is a collection of commercial roofing industry experts dedicated to providing an open forum for discussion, education, and innovation. We provide ongoing resources and expertise for contractors, architects, and building owners.
We are the leading authority in single-ply roofing. Our network deals exclusively with thermosets, thermoplastics, and modified bitumens. Here, you’ll find easy access to online publications and documents that range from industry standards, generic technical guidelines for design and application to general information about roof maintenance and emergency repairs.
 What's SPRI Working On?
 Who is SPRI?
Regular Members manufacture or market flexible sheet membrane roofing systems; but not including independent manufacturers’ representatives or distributors.
Associate Members manufacture and market, or simply market, raw materials, components, accessories, tools or equipment used in flexible sheet membrane roofing systems.
Affiliate Members are professional roof consultants, architectural firms, specifiers, product distributors, sales representatives, testing agencies and research agencies.

 Representing Roof Coatings Manufacturers, Suppliers, and Contractors
 RCMA is the leading industry voice, promoting the benefits of roof coatings and providing its membership with up-to-date information on building codes and standards, technical developments, and other industry topics of interest.
 Education
 Member Benefits
 Roof Coating Resources
 International Roof Coatings Day 
International Roof Coatings Day is an annual observance that raises awareness of the important role roof coatings play in both new roofing projects and roof restoration. 
Roof coatings can help extend the life of existing roofs and may provide benefits such as improved energy efficiency, reduced waste, and support for more sustainable communities, while the day celebrates the people, products, and innovations that help protect and restore roofs around the world.
More information about the holiday will be coming soon.
 Roof Coatings are Essential
 Roof coatings are designed for protecting and extending the useful service life of roof assemblies for new construction and existing roof coverings.
Roof coatings are applied to low slope roofs on residential, commercial, and industrial buildings to extend the life of a roof by preventing water, chemical, or physical damage which saves money for the building owner. Roof coatings are also the most effective and least costly option to help buildings save energy and enhance sustainability.

 Join the Roof Coatings Manufacturers Association as a Contractor Member
 Be part of a national network shaping the future of the roof coatings industry — advance your expertise, stay current on industry advancements, and grow your business.
 Join Today!
 Who is This Membership For?
 Contractors and applicators who specialize in roof coatings, restoration, and maintenance — or those looking to expand their services into roof coating applications. RCMA’s Contractor Membership connects you directly to the industry’s leading manufacturers, suppliers, and technical experts.
 What is the purpose?
 RCMA created this category to ensure that the voice of the professional contractor is represented in discussions about standards, advocacy, education, and best practices.
 Key Benefits – RCMA's Contractor Tool Box
 Advocacy & Representation
Stay informed and have a voice in codes, regulations, and legislative issues that impact your business.
 Technical Resources
Access technical bulletins, white papers, and updates from RCMA’s Technical Affairs Committee.
 Education & Training
Stay ahead with industry webinars, workshops, and standards education on coatings application and compliance.
 Networking & Collaboration
Build connections with manufacturers, suppliers, and other contractors at RCMA meetings and events.
 Set Yourself Apart
Be recognized as a professional and have access to tools to help grow your business.
 Marketing Exposure
Get listed in RCMA’s public Contractor Member Directory and leverage opportunities for project spotlights.
 Membership Requirements
 Differentiate your Business with RCMA
As a contractor in the roof coatings industry, your voice matters. The Roof Coatings Manufacturers Association (RCMA) empowers contractors like you to shape the future of roofing through:
Commitment to safe and sustainable application practices.
Agreement to abide by RCMA’s Code of Conduct and Membership Guidelines.
 Join Today!
Membership in the Roof Coatings Manufacturers Association (RCMA) does not constitute certification, licensure, or accreditation. RCMA membership signifies support for the association’s mission and commitment to industry collaboration. Still, it does not imply endorsement or approval by RCMA of any member or its products, services, or business practices.

 Who We Are 
 Since the early 1960’s, EPDM single-ply rubber membrane roofing products have gained wide industry acceptance and respect by providing long-term, economically efficient, dependable roofing solutions for the construction community. Their attributes include long-term warranties, low life-cycle costs, reduced labor costs, minimal maintenance and user-friendly code approvals. The sustained growth of EPDM roofing systems is attributed to the development of complementary technologies that have made it possible for EPDM roofing systems to be beneficial in a wide number of applications. Architects and contractors have come to depend on this proven track record of performance. As environmentalists and code regulators place more emphasis on the long-term performance of building materials, EPDM has become an increasingly obvious choice. The need to provide the construction and roofing communities with current and accurate data documenting the many benefits of EPDM roofing systems led to the formation of the trade association entitled, the EPDM Roofing Association.
Members of ERA first began discussions about establishing the trade association in 2002 and ERA formally established itself in 2003.  
 BALLASTED EPDM ROOFS
 The EPDM (ethylene propylene diene terpolymer) single-ply rubber roofing membrane has been an appealing choice of the low-slope commercial roofing industry for over 40 years.
The number one roofing choice of architects, roof consultants and contractors for both new construction and replacement roofing projects according to market surveys from Building Design and Construction, and Roofing/Siding/Insulation magazines, and the National Roofing Contractors Association (NRCA).

 Lightweight Fillers for Sustainable, Durable Joint Designs
 Wednesday, November 11, 2026
 10:00 AM - 11:00 AM (EST)
 You will receive an email with a link to the GoToWebinar form once your registration is processed
 Register Now
Event Details
Overview:
Lightweight fillers in sealants enable density reduction, improved workability, and cost optimization while maintaining key mechanical and durability performance in building joints. This webinar will outline formulation strategies, performance tradeoffs, and application considerations for incorporating such fillers into high-performance sealants. Architectural sealants for curtain walls, precast panels, and glazing are increasingly engineered with lightweight inorganic and polymeric fillers, such as expanded perlite, polymeric/hollow microspheres, hollow ceramic microspheres, hollow glass microspheres and other technologies, to reduce density and increase yield without compromising or having minimal impact to movement capability, weatherability and other key properties. By tailoring particle size distribution, compressibility, crush strength, and surface treatment, formulators can control rheology, sag resistance, and thermal insulation while limiting water uptake and maintaining long-term joint integrity. This webinar will review selection criteria for lightweight fillers in silicone, polyurethane, water-based and hybrid sealant chemistries; discuss interactions with thixotropes and plasticizers; and present case data demonstrating impacts on rheology, density, strength properties, cost, VOC and application properties. Implementation guidelines covering mixing and dispersion, quality control of filler properties, and alignment with relevant sealant design standards will be highlighted to support the robust use of lightweight fillers in sustainable, durable architectural joint designs.
Who Should Attend:
This is an ideal webinar for professionals in the building and construction industry including those in business as well as technical roles.

ASC Membership FAQs
HOW ARE THE DUES CALCULATED?
We use a formula to calculate annual dues. Dues are based on company sales in North America based on its most recent fiscal year. Each company reports those sales confidentially to the ASC and we apply that number to dues brackets that have been established that range from sales of less than $500,000 to over $600 million. Corporate dues are then calculated based on these reported sales relative to these brackets.
WHAT IF MY COMPANY IS BOTH A MANUFACTURER OF ADHESIVES/SEALANTS AND A RAW MATERIAL SUPPLIER?
ASC asks that companies combine their sales of all industry related products for the purposes of calculating one's dues. Typically, such companies apply as Manufacturer Members in this case because this member classes does afford a few additional benefits over other member classes. 
DO DUES VARY BY MEMBERSHIP CLASS?
Yes, Manufacturer and Supplier member dues are based on the same schedule. Affiliate members (i.e. adhesive/sealant distributors, consultants and non-North American business entities) are based on a different schedule.
DOES ASC LOBBY?
Advocacy is one of ASC's strategic priorities. We engage federal, state, and local regulatory agencies to represent the voice of the North American adhesive and sealant value chain. When necessary, we meet with elected officials and submit written public comments and/or letters stating our position(s) on a regulatory issue. Our engagement with members of Congress is limited. However, we leverage our relationships with allied associations and work with them to further a congressional issue when the need arises.  
WHY SHOULD A RAW MATERIAL SUPPLIER BE A MEMBER?
From a business development standpoint, this is the one membership a raw material supplier should have. With most of the large adhesive manufacturers represented in the ASC membership, our conventions and networking functions provide a forum for face-to-face interaction with these customers or prospects. We also provide a three-hour EXPO at each of our conventions which gives each supplier the opportunity to showcase their products to all of the attending manufacturer representatives. This is the only show of its kind in the country. Suppliers also have the opportunity to serve on ASC member committees and work collaboratively with adhesive manufacturers to address an industry issue and help accelerate the adoption of adhesives and sealants to downstream end users.
CAN INDIVIDUALS JOIN ASC?
Membership in the ASC is a corporate membership with every employee of a member company given membership benefits. In this way each individual can select those activities that are most important to them to become involved in.
IS ASC JUST FOR TECHNICAL PROFESSIONALS?
The ASC membership has many benefits for all employees of a member company irrespective of job function. We have programs, courses webinars and committees that technical as well as business staff will gain from. It also does not matter whether you are in senior management or just getting started. There is something for everyone on the professional as well as the personal level.
WHO IS IN YOUR ASSOCIATION?
The ASC is a true representation of the industry as our membership is comprised of large, medium and small adhesive manufacturers and raw material suppliers. These companies range from family-owned businesses to the multinational conglomerates. ASC members account for more than 75% of the aggregate industry revenues, exceeding some $16+ billion annually.
HOW IS ASC GOVERNED?
A 22-member Board of Directors governs the ASC, in accordance with ASC's bylaws, and provides strategic guidance and vision. Directors represent a mix of Manufacturer and Supplier members, both large and small. Each Director serves a three-year term, which can be renewed.
HOW CAN I GET INVOLVED IN COUNCIL ACTIVITIES?
There are many ways to participate, ranging from committees, government relations task forces, technical committees, peer groups, and much more.
DOES ASC HAVE CHAPTERS AROUND THE WORLD?
No, the ASC's only office is in suburban Washington, DC. ASC does maintain close relations with other regional associations such as in Europe and Asia, but these organizations are not formally affiliations.
DOES ASC HAVE A “NEW MEMBER” REFERRAL PROGRAM?
YES, ASC does have a new member referral program. It is available to current ASC Members only, Any employee of a current ASC member company can submit, regardless of title or role. Simply email Brian Peters, Director of Membership & Industry Programs at brian.peters@ascouncil.org with the following information: referred company's name; and name/title/e-mail/phone number, of an individual at the company. Special recognition will be given to the individual and company referring a new member when the new member joins ASC.
Thank you for your interest in joining the Adhesive and Sealant Council. To start the membership process, or if you have questions regarding ASC membership, please email Brian Peters or call (301) 986-9739.

 ACA Partners with Vincentz Network to Expand CoatingsTech through New Digital Platform
 September 8, 2026
 ACA has entered into an agreement with Vincentz Network (Vincentz) to expand and enhance its CoatingsTech publication through a new digital-first format. CoatingsTech — which ACA had produced as six printed issues annually, with an accompanying biweekly enewsletter, CoatingsTech Direct — will now be produced by Vincentz Network for ACA as an augmented, weekly e-newsletter with accompanying digital platform.

 August Names in the News
 August 24, 2026
 ACA welcomes David Bloomgren as its Director of External Communications, effective Aug. 24, 2026. Bloomgren’s extensive public affairs and strategic communications experience encompasses roles across government and industry, including serving as a senior advisor to two U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrators during the Obama Administration, as well as serving as Communications Director for both the Office of Air and Radiation and the Office of Enforcement and Compliance Assurance. 
 ACA-supported 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act Becomes Law
 July 14, 2026
 On July 11, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act — a landmark bipartisan housing package that ACA championed — became law. ACA had actively supported and advocated for legislation that will expand and preserve the country's housing supply, improve housing affordability, and drive job growth. 
 Compliance Date for National Aerosol Rule Moved to January 2027
 July 7, 2025
 On July 2, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) published in the Federal Register interim final action to revise the compliance date in the recent amendments to the national aerosol coatings rule. In response to industry concerns, EPA is delaying the compliance date from July 17, 2025, to Jan. 17, 2027. 
 PHMSA Issues Notices of Proposed Rulemaking Aimed at Reducing Regulatory Burdens
 July 7, 2025
 On July 1, the U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) issued several notices of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) in the Federal Register aimed at reducing existing regulatory burdens that impact our industry. Notably, one of the NPRMs responds to a petition ACA filed in 2017. 
 California’s DTSC Proposes to Add Microplastics to Candidate Chemicals List of Safer Consumer Products Program
 July 7, 2025
 California’s Department of Toxic Substances (DTSC) is proposing a definition of microplastics, and the addition of microplastics to the candidate chemicals list under California’s Safer Consumer Products Program. The agency is accepting comments on the proposal through Aug. 4, 2025. 
 SCAQMD Public Hearing for Proposed Amendments to Solvent Cleaning Operations Rule Set for June 6
 May 12, 2025
 California’s South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD) on May 6 issued a notice of public hearing for Proposed Amended Rule 1171 (Solvent Cleaning Operations). The district has also published the draft rule language and draft staff report on its website.

 August 7, 2026
 HydroGraph Clean Power Inc. announced that its U.S. subsidiary, HydroGraph USA Inc., has executed definitive agreements with Western International Gas & Cylinders, Inc. to secure a long-term supply of acetylene gas and lease land for HydroGraph’s first large-scale U.S. graphene production facility, to be located in Bellville, Texas. 
 Elinor Coatings Achieves ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D (2016) Certification
 August 7, 2026
 Elinor Coatings has received ISO 9001:2015 and AS9100D (2016) certification. The certifications, issued by Performance Review Institute (PRI), confirm that Elinor Coatings’ quality management system meets the requirements of general industry under ISO 9001:2015 and the specialized needs of aviation, space and defense organizations under AS9100D (20216).

 August 7, 2026
 OXERRA Group has announced plans to expand its Complex Inorganic Colour Pigments (CICP) platform in China. The investment adds 4,000 metric tonnes of manufacturing capacity and supports OXERRA's long-term CICP roadmap.

 Registration Is Open for the Autumn Regional Meeting
 Timely education. Meaningful connections. Practical solutions.
 Join ACD this September for the 2026 Autumn Regional Meeting, where chemical distribution professionals will come together for a full day of education, networking, and conversations focused on the issues shaping our industry.
 Whether you're looking to stay informed on emerging trends, exchange ideas with peers, or expand your professional network, the Autumn Regional Meeting offers valuable insights and connections to help move your business forward.
 We look forward to seeing you in Morristown this September.

 Explore ACD's New and Improved Regulatory Resource Guide
 A constantly shifting regulatory outlook can be difficult to navigate. ACD is here to help.
Our regulatory team works constantly to keep members informed about the latest regulations and policies affecting the chemical distribution industry, so your regulatory compliance teams can make confident, well-informed decisions. One of the key tools we offer members is the Regulatory Resource Guide, a centralized document where you can find up-to-date regulatory compliance information.

 After you’ve entered the user portal, switch to the company profile by clicking on the profile icon in the top right corner of the user portal page.

 Selecting the membership dues renewal invoice from the list of invoices and clicking the pay button will take you through the process for applying payment.
If your current username and password does not generate a successful login, and you are still unsuccessful after attempting to reset your password, then your company's membership is most likely expired. Memberships that are not renewed annually by April 1 are considered expired. BSCAI welcomes back all expired members.

If you have any other questions about your membership renewal, please contact info@bscai.org.

 About RIA
 The Restoration Industry Association
 is the oldest and largest non-profit, professional trade association dedicated to providing leadership and promoting best practices through advocacy, standards & professional qualifications for the restoration industry.
 Read More
 Educate.
 RIA provides in-person and on-demand education options for restoration professionals seeking to level-up in their career. Whether you are pursuing or working to maintain certification, RIA education courses and programs can help you earn the continuing education credits you need.
 Learn More
 Advocate.
 RIA’s Advocacy and Government Affairs (AGA) committee is the restoration industry’s first unified advocacy team. It seeks to unite the restoration industry, advocate for the best interests of restoration contractors nationwide, and develop and implement strategies to help create and maintain equity between restorers and insurers and their partners.
 Learn More
 Elevate.
 RIA works tirelessly to increase the credibility of the restoration industry and its professionals through education, advocacy, and events to maximize industry exposure. With an extensive network of professionals working toward similar goals, RIA has become a trusted resource of knowledge for those involved in cleaning and restoration.
 Learn More
 Become a Member
 Broaden your business opportunities, strengthen your training programs and promote your professionalism to the industry and beyond.
 Join Today

What did I like about the FLS? The FLS takes all of the knowledge that you have relating to fire restoration (in my case over 20 years’ worth and I’ve forgotten some) and builds on it. Sharing the unique experience and challenges of the FLS with a group of highly motivated people has given me bonds with my peers who are leaders and experts in their field. As a CR, I know that these bonds become friendships and they’ll always be there to share their expertise and I’ll be there for them too. I love a challenge and the FLS delivered. If you love a challenge and If you want to raise the bar and be recognized as a leader in the field of Fire Loss then the new RIA FLS Certification is for you.

Join the RIA - Membership Your Way!
 The Restoration Industry Association (RIA) is the oldest and largest non-profit trade association supporting professionals in the restoration and reconstruction industry. We are uniting contractors, vendors, and industry leaders while advocating for equity in the insurance ecosystem and advancing the profession through education, networking, and resources.
Whether you are a contractor, vendor, or industry professional, there is an RIA membership option that fits your needs, goals, and business stage.
Why Join RIA?
As an RIA member, you gain exclusive access to tools and resources that help you:
✅ Grow your business and expand opportunities✅ Streamline your training and upskill your team✅ Advocate for fair treatment in the insurance ecosystem✅ Connect with restoration leaders across North America✅ Save on products and services you use daily
Your Membership Benefits Include:
As an RIA member, you gain exclusive access to tools and resources that help you:
As a member of the RIA you will have access to many benefits to help broaden your business opportunities, strengthen your training programs and promote your professionalism to the industry and beyond. You'll also receive substantial discounts and savings on products and services you use everyday in your business!
RIA Convention & Industry ExpoThe RIA Convention is the must-attend event for restoration contractors looking to grow their business. Join over 900 restoration leaders to network, learn proven strategies, and explore the latest tools and technology in a 120+ booth expo hall. Walk away with new connections, actionable insights, and resources to drive your business forward. As an RIA member, you’ll save $200 on your registration—adding even more ROI to your investment.
Register Today
Advocacy (AGA) ResourcesRIA’s AGA program fights for fair treatment and faster payment for restoration contractors. We advocate on your behalf while building productive relationships with insurers and industry stakeholders. As a member, you get access to exclusive AGA resources—position statements, training videos, and practical tools—to help you get paid faster and navigate the insurance claims process with confidence.
Learn More
Advanced Designations & TrainingTake your career and business to the next level with RIA’s industry-leading designations: CR, FLS, CLS, WLS, and ERS. RIA members save over $300 on advanced training courses, available on-demand and in-person, covering essential technical and leadership skills. Invest in your expertise while saving money—and stand out in the restoration industry.
LEARN MORE
Regional Networking EventsJoin fellow restorers in your region to network, gain business insights from industry leaders to help improve your bottom line, hear from RIA's Restoration Advocate, Ed Cross, on the RIA's advocacy efforts on behalf of restorers and much more. RIA members receive discounted rates on registration.
LEARN MORE
Labor CalculatorRIA membership provides you free access to the Labor Calculator created by JRCC and Enlightened Restoration Solutions to help contractors understand pricing (a $100 value). This proprietary labor rate calculator will help you create your own price list.
LEARN MORE
Discounts on Products & ServicesRIA’s Affinity Partner Program helps you cut costs on the products and services you use daily. By leveraging the association’s buying power, RIA members get exclusive discounts and rebates that can save you thousands each year. On average, contractors who participate in just two programs save at least $1,600 annually. Every dollar you save also supports RIA’s mission, as Affinity Partners give back to RIA based on member participation. It’s a win-win for your business and your industry.
 LEARN MORE
Find a Pro Directory ListingGet Found. Win More Work.Stand out from the competition and attract new customers with RIA’s Find a Pro Directory. This searchable tool helps consumers and industry partners find and choose your services, making it easier for potential clients to connect with your business.
LEARN MORE
Restoration Blog & Industry UpdatesStay Ahead with Industry InsightsRIA members get exclusive access to the latest restoration news, AGA advocacy updates, and new legislative alerts through the RIA Industry Insights e-newsletter and Restoration Blog. Stay informed, make smarter business decisions, and stay ahead of industry changes.
LEARN MORE
The RIA qualifies as a tax-exempt organization pursuant to Section 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code. Therefore, dues to the RIA are not deductible as a charitable contribution for federal tax purposes but may be deductible as an ordinary and necessary business expense to the extent that they do not pertain to lobbying or political activities. Please consult your tax advisor.
RIA Membership Options
The RIA offers several different membership categories, each with easy and affordable payment options. Please note that membership dues are nonrefundable. RIA membership dues may be tax deductible as an ordinary and necessary business expense. The RIA estimates that 10% of your 2025 membership dues is not deductible due to lobbying expenses. Please consult your tax advisor for further information.
First Time Contractor Member DiscountFirst-time contractor members (or those lapsed 3+ years) are eligible for a discounted first-year rate of $299 or $25 a month.
Learn More
Contractor MemberFor companies directly providing restoration, mitigation, cleaning, reconstruction, and related services to structures or contents.
Learn More 
Individual Professional MemberOpen to any individual in solitary practice providing services involving the restoration, mitigation, reconstruction, remediation, abatement, environmental, cleaning, or similar services to the built environment or its contents; or any individual with an interest in the restoration industry; or technical consultants, facility managers, restaurants, hospitals, universities, municipalities and other related organizations. This option is only available to US based members.
Learn More 
Enterprise MemberOpen to regional, national or international companies who have multiple locations. This company shall be engaged in providing services involving the restoration, mitigation, reconstruction, remediation, abatement, environmental, cleaning, or similar services to the built environment or its contents.
Learn More 
Franchisor/Franchisee MemberOpen to regional, national or international companies who franchise their business model as well as provide corporate locations. This company shall be engaged in providing services involving the restoration, mitigation, reconstruction, remediation, abatement, environmental, cleaning, or similar services to the built environment or its contents. 
To join as a Franchisor/Franchisee Member, contact us at 856-439-9222 or info@restorationindustry.org.
Learn More
Vendor MemberDefined as any company engaged in the manufacture, sale, installation and/or distribution of products and services used by members, but not directly engaged in the cleaning and/or restoration business. 
To join as a Vendor Member, please contact Amanda Bray, Industry Relations Manager at 856-437-4750 or abray@restorationindustry.org.
Learn More
Australasian MemberAustralian & New Zealand members must join through our affiliate organization, RIA Australasia.
Learn More 
Guest AccountA nonmember guest account may be granted to any individual wishing to make a purchase through the RIA website for store orders, events and training. Guest accounts do not have access to RIA member benefits or member pricing.
Create Guest Account
Join the community that is shaping the future of the restoration industry while unlocking resources, advocacy, and tools to strengthen your business every day or contact us at info@restorationindustry.org for assistance in selecting the best membership option for you.

You'll also receive substantial discounts and savings on products and services you use everyday in your business!
RIA Convention & Industry ExpoThe RIA Convention is the must-attend event for restoration contractors looking to grow their business. Join over 900 restoration leaders to network, learn proven strategies, and explore the latest tools and technology in a 120+ booth expo hall. Walk away with new connections, actionable insights, and resources to drive your business forward. As an RIA member, you’ll save $200 on your registration—adding even more ROI to your investment.
Register Today
Advocacy (AGA) ResourcesRIA’s AGA program fights for fair treatment and faster payment for restoration contractors. We advocate on your behalf while building productive relationships with insurers and industry stakeholders. As a member, you get access to exclusive AGA resources—position statements, training videos, and practical tools—to help you get paid faster and navigate the insurance claims process with confidence.
Learn More
Advanced Designations & TrainingTake your career and business to the next level with RIA’s industry-leading designations: CR, FLS, CLS, WLS, and ERS. RIA members save over $300 on advanced training courses, available on-demand and in-person, covering essential technical and leadership skills. Invest in your expertise while saving money—and stand out in the restoration industry.
LEARN MORE
Regional Networking EventsJoin fellow restorers in your region to network, gain business insights from industry leaders to help improve your bottom line, hear from RIA's Restoration Advocate, Ed Cross, on the RIA's advocacy efforts on behalf of restorers and much more. RIA members receive discounted rates on registration.
LEARN MORE
Labor CalculatorRIA membership provides you free access to the Labor Calculator created by JRCC and Enlightened Restoration Solutions to help contractors understand pricing (a $100 value). This proprietary labor rate calculator will help you create your own price list.
LEARN MORE
Discounts on Products & ServicesRIA’s Affinity Partner Program helps you cut costs on the products and services you use daily. By leveraging the association’s buying power, RIA members get exclusive discounts and rebates that can save you thousands each year. On average, contractors who participate in just two programs save at least $1,600 annually. Every dollar you save also supports RIA’s mission, as Affinity Partners give back to RIA based on member participation. It’s a win-win for your business and your industry.
 LEARN MORE
Find a Pro Directory ListingGet Found. Win More Work.Stand out from the competition and attract new customers with RIA’s Find a Pro Directory. This searchable tool helps consumers and industry partners find and choose your services, making it easier for potential clients to connect with your business.
LEARN MORE
Restoration Blog & Industry UpdatesStay Ahead with Industry InsightsRIA members get exclusive access to the latest restoration news, AGA advocacy updates, and new legislative alerts through the RIA Industry Insights e-newsletter and Restoration Blog. Stay informed, make smarter business decisions, and stay ahead of industry changes.
LEARN MORE
The RIA qualifies as a tax-exempt organization pursuant to Section 501(c)(6) of the Internal Revenue Code. Therefore, dues to the RIA are not deductible as a charitable contribution for federal tax purposes but may be deductible as an ordinary and necessary business expense to the extent that they do not pertain to lobbying or political activities. Please consult your tax advisor.
RIA Membership Options
The RIA offers several different membership categories, each with easy and affordable payment options. Please note that membership dues are nonrefundable. RIA membership dues may be tax deductible as an ordinary and necessary business expense. The RIA estimates that 10% of your 2025 membership dues is not deductible due to lobbying expenses. Please consult your tax advisor for further information.
First Time Contractor Member DiscountFirst-time contractor members (or those lapsed 3+ years) are eligible for a discounted first-year rate of $299 or $25 a month.
Learn More
Contractor MemberFor companies directly providing restoration, mitigation, cleaning, reconstruction, and related services to structures or contents.
Learn More 
Individual Professional MemberOpen to any individual in solitary practice providing services involving the restoration, mitigation, reconstruction, remediation, abatement, environmental, cleaning, or similar services to the built environment or its contents; or any individual with an interest in the restoration industry; or technical consultants, facility managers, restaurants, hospitals, universities, municipalities and other related organizations. This option is only available to US based members.
Learn More 
Enterprise MemberOpen to regional, national or international companies who have multiple locations. This company shall be engaged in providing services involving the restoration, mitigation, reconstruction, remediation, abatement, environmental, cleaning, or similar services to the built environment or its contents.
Learn More 
Franchisor/Franchisee MemberOpen to regional, national or international companies who franchise their business model as well as provide corporate locations. This company shall be engaged in providing services involving the restoration, mitigation, reconstruction, remediation, abatement, environmental, cleaning, or similar services to the built environment or its contents. 
To join as a Franchisor/Franchisee Member, contact us at 856-439-9222 or info@restorationindustry.org.
Learn More
Vendor MemberDefined as any company engaged in the manufacture, sale, installation and/or distribution of products and services used by members, but not directly engaged in the cleaning and/or restoration business. 
To join as a Vendor Member, please contact Amanda Bray, Industry Relations Manager at 856-437-4750 or abray@restorationindustry.org.
Learn More
Australasian MemberAustralian & New Zealand members must join through our affiliate organization, RIA Australasia.
Learn More 
Guest AccountA nonmember guest account may be granted to any individual wishing to make a purchase through the RIA website for store orders, events and training. Guest accounts do not have access to RIA member benefits or member pricing.
Create Guest Account
Join the community that is shaping the future of the restoration industry while unlocking resources, advocacy, and tools to strengthen your business every day or contact us at info@restorationindustry.org for assistance in selecting the best membership option for you.

From our trade shows Winter FancyFaire* and the Summer Fancy Food Show to the sofi Awards to research reports and more, SFA benefits connect and champion our member companies and support the growing specialty food industry.
If you're not a member yet, SFA invites you to learn more on this page. You can also always reach us at [email protected] with any questions.

Joining PFI puts your company on the cutting edge of pet food policy and advocacy. However, more than most trade orgs, we actively help our members solve problems while bringing people and companies together to foster innovation and move our industry forward.
Our 2025 Highlights
Analyzed 4,000+ bills, tracked more than 650, monitored 200+ priority bills, and followed 160+ packaging/plastics/environmental bills
Tracked more than 100 federal bills in the 119th Congress
Proactively engaged in advocacy efforts in all 50 states
Provided real-time support on tariffs and trade disruptions
Participated in USDA programs to expand market access and grow exports
Offered consumer-facing education on label modernization
View 2025 Impact Report
Our Impact 2025
100+Federal bills tracked in Congress
4,000Analyzed nearly 4,000 state measures across the U.S.
600+State bills tracked and monitored
75+Congressional offices engaged with
Membership Categories
Membership in PFI is determined by the type of business you conduct within the pet food or adjacent industries.
Producer Member
Manufactures commercially prepared dog and/or cat food and/or treats in the U.S.
Follow a strict Code of Practice as a commitment to responsibility and integrity. 
Learn More
Associate Member
Supplies goods or services to support production of dog and/or cat food and/or treats.
Markets and distributes commercially produced dog and/or cat food and/or treats within the U.S. under your own name or trade name for sale in retail outlets, but aren’t primarily in the business of selling goods directly to consumers.

Are you looking for an organization where you can connect with others in the same industry while making your voice heard among lawmakers at the state and national levels? Do you want to know there is somewhere to turn, with experts you can trust, when your company is seeking answers to difficult industry-related questions? And is it important to you and your company to receive up-to-date industry information from an organization that specializes only in animal food? The American Feed Industry Association has provided all of those member benefits and more for more than 100 years to companies searching for just that!
AFIA is the largest trade association representing the feed industry. Aside from being the “Voice of the Total Feed Industry,” AFIA will provide an excellent resource for your company to network with the most influential companies in animal feed, pet food and livestock production. AFIA hosts the largest animal feed trade show in the world, the International Feed Expo, which is part of the International Production & Processing Expo, as well as the largest animal feed and pet food ingredient conference in the world, the Purchasing and Ingredient Suppliers Conference – both excellent opportunities for your company to network and conduct business.
If your company aims to stay informed about the regulatory landscape affecting the animal food industry, AFIA's expert staff and comprehensive resources are unmatched. From navigating state feed registrations to understanding the Food Safety Modernization Act rules, and complying with regulations from OSHA and the EPA, AFIA provides the guidance you need to maintain your competitive edge. 
Join AFIA today to ensure your company remains at the forefront of industry developments and regulatory changes. 
We make four promises to our members:
 You will have a voice as part of the total feed industry association;
 We will provide expert legislative and regulatory leadership and representation;
 We offer confidential individual staff expertise on demand; and
 We provide engagement opportunities for specialized training, professional education and networking.
For feed manufacturers (both commercial and integrated) and pet food manufacturers, the dues are based on U.S. manufactured tonnage. For ingredient suppliers, equipment manufacturers and industry support, the dues are based on the dollar sales in the U.S. The minimum dues for an AFIA membership is $2,500 per year.
For more information, contact Jennie Cameron, AFIA’s director of membership and engagement, at jcameron@afia.org.

 Join PIDA
 All applications are subject to review and approval by the PIDA Board of Directors. 
Applications must be completed in their entirety for consideration — incomplete applications will not be considered.  
Forward membership applications to nbull@pida.org.
Distributor Membership
Click here to download the application form.
Any entity that is a wholesale-distributor of multi-brands of manufactured pet products (including pet food) to independent pet retailers* shall be eligible for Distributor Membership. The Board of Directors (or its delegees) shall have discretion to determine whether an applicant shall be admitted as a Distributor Member based on all the facts and circumstances, including, but not limited to:
 The number of manufactures whose products are sold by the applicant to independent retailers.
 The length of time the applicant has been in business as a wholesale distributor of pet products.
 The number of independent retailers that recognize the applicant as a wholesale distributor of pet products.
 The size and nature of the applicant’s warehouse facility and its location with respect to any retail pet outlet.
 The type of catalog or merchandise listing that the applicant uses in the sale of the products it distributes.
 The nature of the applicant’s sales staff and other services provided to customers.
 The methods that the applicant uses to deliver products to customers.
*For the purposes of these R&Rs, the term “independent retailers” shall not include any retail outlet in which the applicant or any officer, director, employee or partner of the applicant has any direct or indirect financial interest other than through the sale of pet products or pets (as applicable).
Pet Wholesaler Membership
Click here to download the application form.
Any entity that is a recognized wholesale distributor of pets or live animal feed that is not principally engaged in the sale and distribution of pet products shall be eligible for Pet Wholesaler Membership.  The Board of Directors (or its delegees) shall have discretion to determine whether an applicant shall be admitted as a Pet Wholesaler Member based on all the facts and circumstances, including, but not limited to:
 The source of the applicant’s pets,
 The length of time the applicant has been in business as a wholesale distributor of pets or live animal feed.
 The number of independent retailers who recognize the applicant as a wholesale distributor of pets or live animal feed.
 Whether or not the applicant maintains permanent holding facilities* designed for the housing, conditioning and humane care of animals.
 Whether the applicant maintains a sales staff and publishes pet inventory lists.
 Whether the applicant possesses the requisite state, local and federal licenses, regulations or permits for purchasing, holding, selling or distributing pets.
Any entity that is engaged in trans-shipment activities shall not be eligible for Pet Wholesaler Membership. 
*For the purposes of these R&Rs, the term “holding facility” shall not include vehicles, trailers or the utilization of common carrier facilities for housing, processing and/or trans-shipping.
Manufacturer Membership
Click here to download the application form.
Manufacturer Membership is offered to any entity that
 A recognized seller of pet products to wholesaler distributors.
 Provides printed or electronic catalogues or merchandise listings.
 Maintains a sales team or independent representatives.
 Has shipped products to pet product wholesaler distributors for a minimum of 12 months prior to applying for membership in the Corporation.
The Board of Directors (or its delegees) shall have discretion to determine whether an applicant shall be admitted as a Manufacturer Member. 
Manufacturer Representative Membership
Click here to download the application form.
Any person or entity who/that is a recognized representative of a manufacture or of an entity providing services or products to wholesale distributors in the pet industry is eligible for Manufacturer Representative Membership.   
The Board of Directors (or its delegees) shall have discretion to determine whether an applicant shall be admitted as a Manufacturer Representative Member. 
Associate Membership
Click here to download the application form.
Any person or entity who/that is a member of the pet industry trade press or who/that sells non-pet products or services (e.g., technology, insurance) to pet industry wholesaler distributors or retailers shall be eligible for Associate Membership.  Persons and entities that merely supply raw materials or packaging products to manufacturers of pet products are not eligible for Association Membership.
The Board of Directors (or its delegees) shall have discretion to determine whether an applicant shall be admitted as an Associate Member.

 About
We are your connected community of organic innovators and pioneers. Our path forward is organic.
The Organic Trade Association (OTA) is the leading membership-based business association representing the U.S. organic sector. Our members span the entire organic supply chain, including growers, processors, certifiers, retailers, and others dedicated to advancing organic agriculture and trade. Our mission is to grow and protect organic through a unified voice that serves and engages our diverse membership from farm to marketplace.

 About the Organic Trade Association
The Organic Trade Association (OTA) is the membership-based business association for organic agriculture and products in North America. OTA is the leading voice for the organic trade in the United States, representing organic businesses and producers across the nation. Its members include growers, shippers, processors, certifiers, farmers' associations, distributors, importers, exporters, consultants, brands, retailers and others. OTA's mission is to promote and protect ORGANIC with a unifying voice that serves and engages its diverse members from farm to marketplace. Our member businesses work together through networking, advocacy, and other initiatives to encourage and protect organic farming practices and to share messages about the positive environmental and nutritional attributes of organic products with consumers, the media, and policymakers. 
We are a connected community of innovators and pioneers working to shape the future for organic food and farming. Together, with our members, we are focused on solutions.

 Membership
 The Organic Trade Association (OTA) is the leading voice for the U.S. organic sector, representing a diverse and vibrant membership—from growers and processors to certifiers, distributors, retailers, and more.
Whether you're a startup brand, family farm, or global company, OTA connects you to a powerful network committed to advancing organic agriculture and protecting the integrity of the organic label.
Questions about membership? Contact Danielle Cote, OTA’s Member Engagement Manager, at dcote@ota.com or (202) 524-3896.
Who Are Our Members?
Our members include:
Organic producers and growers
Processors and manufacturers
Certifiers and industry consultants
Retailers and distributors
Importers, exporters, and farmers’ associations
Together, we champion organic through advocacy, research, networking, education, and strategic marketing—raising the profile of organic with consumers, media, and policymakers.
OTA Members Listing
5 Reasons to Join OTA Today: 
1) Regulatory Expertise: Get personalized support and up-to-date guidance on organic regulations and certification to protect and grow your business.
2) Advocacy & Policy Influence: Shape the future of organic by engaging directly with elected officials and decision-makers on Capitol Hill.
3) Marketing Support & Visibility: Gain access to exclusive tools, promotions, and directory listings to expand your reach with customers and supply chain partners.
4) Media & Crisis Communications Access: Leverage OTA’s strong media relationships and experienced communications team for brand visibility and crisis support.
5) Market Intelligence: Stay ahead with proprietary OTA market research, trends, and insights to inform your strategy and growth.
Ready to Learn More? 
We’re here to help! Choose the option that works best for you:
Option 1: Contact Danielle Cote, OTA’s Member Engagement Manager at dcote@ota.com or (202) 524-3896.
Option 2: Request an email follow-up: Fill out the form below and we'll be in touch.

 California passes muscle/weight dietary supplement age restriction law
September 29, 2026
The Governor of California has signed Assembly Bill 2030, an age restriction bill targeting a loosely defined category of active nutrition dietary supplements.
Under the new law, dietary supplements “labeled, marketed, or otherwise represented” for weight loss or musclebuilding cannot be sold to those under 18 beginning January 1, 2027. Delivery sellers of covered products must either (i) age-verify purchasers via one or more third-party databases regularly used for age and identity verification purposes or (ii) ship covered products to the consumer using a delivery method requiring an adult to sign for the shipment and present government-issued photo identification demonstrating that the recipient is 18 or over. Retail sellers must perform a similar ID check.
Like a similar 2024 New York law, AB 2030 lacks a clear scope of coverage, with language that suggests retail placement, ingredients, or third-party statements could subject a product to age restrictions. Unlike the New York law, no exception exists in AB 2030 for protein products, and enforcement action may be taken by a wide range of public attorneys.
The American Herbal Products Association (AHPA) has held a longstanding position of opposition to state-level, category-specific restriction bills, and AHPA coordinates industry responses to age restriction bills like AB 2030 through the Dietary Supplement Access Coalition.
“Lacking any scientific justification, AB 2030 casts a shadow over safe, beneficial products,” said AHPA Vice President of Regulatory & Government Affairs Robert Marriott. “AHPA and the aligned trade will consider all available legislative, administrative, and legal options to address the many problems this law creates.”

 AHPA launches the “AHPA Atlas,” combining four industry-leading resources into one digital platform
September 22, 2026
The American Herbal Products Association (AHPA) is proud to announce the launch of the AHPA Atlas, an integrated, searchable digital platform that brings together AHPA's most trusted, industry-leading references into one centralized resource.
The AHPA Atlas combines four of AHPA's core, authoritative publications and databases:
 Herbs of Commerce
 Botanical Safety Handbook
 New Dietary Ingredient (NDI) Database
 Botanical Identity (ID) References Compendium
Designed for dietary supplement manufacturers, botanical researchers, regulatory professionals, and companies across the herbal supply chain, the AHPA Atlas provides streamlined digital access to critical nomenclature, safety data, regulatory insights, and analytical identification tools.
"For decades, AHPA has established the benchmark for responsible trade and botanical self-regulation through our industry-leading resources," said AHPA President & CEO Graham Rigby. "The AHPA Atlas represents a massive leap forward, equipping our members and the broader herbal community with an advanced, searchable digital platform that places decades of essential safety and regulatory knowledge directly at their fingertips."
Key features
 Nomenclature & labeling guidance: Lookup authoritative common names, botanical synonyms, and traditional names from Herbs of Commerce to ensure accurate and compliant product labeling.
 Comprehensive safety & regulatory insights: Consult expert-reviewed safety profiles from the Botanical Safety Handbook and search FDA NDI notification records.
 Analytical testing & identification tools: Explore curated physical characteristics, organoleptic descriptions, and testing methodologies via the Botanical ID References Compendium.
 Unified cross-platform searchability: Cross-reference botanical ingredients instantly across all four foundational AHPA resources without switching between resources.
"Consider this just the beginning for the AHPA Atlas," added Rigby. "We are actively expanding the platform, adding new content, features, and functionality as we go to ensure it serves as the definitive digital tool for the industry."
Full access to the AHPA Atlas is included as a benefit of AHPA membership. Members can log in and explore the new platform by visiting ahpa.org/atlas.

 AHPA welcomes introduction of Dietary Supplement Innovation Act
Newly introduced legislation modernizes drug preclusion framework to foster innovation and protect consumer access
September 10, 2026
The American Herbal Products Association (AHPA) welcomes the introduction of the Dietary Supplement Innovation Act by Representative Diana Harshbarger (R-TN). This critical legislation clarifies and modernizes the drug preclusion provision of the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (DSHEA), establishing greater regulatory certainty while preserving consumer access to safe dietary supplement ingredients.
Ambiguity surrounding the interaction between drug development and dietary supplements has long created unnecessary impediments to industry innovation. This new legislation addresses these challenges by clarifying when drug preclusion applies, ensuring that discontinued or inactive drug development programs do not permanently block ingredients from the dietary supplement market. It also ensures that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) can never again attempt to use the provision to remove ingredients that existed in the dietary supplement market prior to DSHEA's enactment. Furthermore, the bill strikes an appropriate balance between protecting pharmaceutical research incentives and allowing consumer access to new dietary supplements, avoiding costly disputes while providing FDA a predictable pathway to resolve issues through an administrative order when appropriate.
“Botanical dietary supplement innovation depends on clearly defined pathways that allow safe herbs and natural products to reach consumers,” said AHPA President & CEO Graham Rigby. “Representative Harshbarger's legislation would help restore the balance Congress intended under DSHEA and better ensure that drug development does not unnecessarily foreclose dietary supplement innovation. AHPA applauds Representative Harshbarger for her leadership and urges Congress to advance this important legislation as a key plank of modernizing the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act's robust dietary supplement provisions.”
Alongside the Consumer Healthcare Products Association (CHPA) and the Council for Responsible Nutrition (CRN), AHPA supports this legislation and will continue working closely with congressional leaders, regulatory agencies, and industry partners to advance a modern, science-based regulatory framework that fosters innovation, provides regulatory certainty, and preserves consumer access to trusted products.

 Dietary Supplement Trades Applaud Legislation to Modernize Drug Preclusion Framework
September 10, 2026
The American Herbal Products Association (AHPA), Consumer Healthcare Products Association (CHPA), and Council for Responsible Nutrition (CRN) welcome today's introduction of the Dietary Supplement Innovation Act, by Rep. Diana Harshbarger (TN-01) to clarify and modernize the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act's (DSHEA's) drug preclusion provision, providing greater regulatory certainty while preserving consumer access to safe dietary supplement ingredients.
“Ambiguous FDA standards can leave manufacturers without guidance and consumers guessing about which products are available,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger. “For decades, this broken drug preclusion process has allowed Washington bureaucrats to threaten lawful dietary supplements that have safely been purchased over the counter for years, stifling innovation and denying Americans access to products they already trust. My bill delivers the regulatory certainty manufacturers need to innovate and invest with confidence, while establishing transparency and predictability within the drug preclusion framework and preserving consumer access to dietary supplements.”
“Botanical dietary supplement innovation depends on clearly defined pathways that allow safe herbs and natural products to reach consumers,” said AHPA President and CEO Graham Rigby. “Representative Harshbarger's legislation would help restore the balance Congress intended under DSHEA and better ensure that drug development does not unnecessarily foreclose legitimate dietary supplement innovation. AHPA applauds Representative Harshbarger for her leadership and urges Congress to advance this important legislation as a key plank of modernizing the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act's robust dietary supplement provisions.”
"We applaud Representative Harshbarger for introducing this important legislation, which modernizes an outdated provision of law, provides much-needed regulatory certainty, and helps ensure consumer access keeps pace with innovation," said CHPA President and CEO Scott Melville. 
"Representative Harshbarger has introduced exactly the kind of thoughtful, balanced legislation this issue has needed for years," said Steve Mister, President and CEO of the Council for Responsible Nutrition. "This bill doesn't weaken FDA or undermine pharmaceutical innovation. Instead, it restores the balance Congress intended when it enacted DSHEA by creating transparent, predictable rules that allow both industries to innovate while protecting consumer access to safe dietary supplements. We commend Representative Harshbarger for her leadership and strongly urge Congress to advance this legislation." 
The legislation would:
 Preserve access to ingredients that were marketed in foods or dietary supplements prior to Oct. 15, 1994.
 Clarify when drug preclusion applies, so ingredients involved in discontinued or inactive drug development programs are not blocked from the dietary supplement market forever.
 Provide greater regulatory predictability for manufacturers, researchers, and consumers.
 Help ensure that innovative ingredients are not unnecessarily excluded from the dietary supplement marketplace when no approved drug reaches the market.
 Strike an appropriate balance between protecting pharmaceutical research and allowing consumer access to new dietary supplements.
 Reduce costly and resource-intensive disputes by providing clearer rules regarding when drug preclusion applies.
 Streamline the pathway for FDA to allow both dietary supplements and drugs with the same ingredient at FDA's discretion under predictable rules and procedures.
Recent consumer research found strong voter support for updating dietary supplement regulations and overwhelming agreement that dietary supplements positively impact health and wellness. The research also found broad support for reforms that strengthen innovation while maintaining consumer protections.
The associations look forward to working with policymakers and stakeholders to advance a modern, science-based regulatory framework that fosters innovation, provides greater regulatory certainty, and preserves access to products that consumers trust.

About American Herbal Products Association
Founded in 1982, the American Herbal Products Association (AHPA) is the national trade association and voice of the herbal products industry, representing growers, processors, manufacturers, and marketers of herbs and herbal products — including foods, dietary supplements, cosmetics, and non-prescription drugs — as well as companies providing expert services to the trade. AHPA champions the responsible and sustainable commerce of safe, high-quality herbal goods to ensure informed consumer access. Learn more at ahpa.org.
About Consumer Healthcare Products Association
The Consumer Healthcare Products Association (CHPA), founded in 1881, is the national trade association representing the leading manufacturers and marketers of consumer healthcare products, including over-the-counter (OTC) medicines, dietary supplements, and consumer medical devices. CHPA is committed to empowering self-care by ensuring that Americans have access to products they can count on to be reliable, affordable, and convenient, while also delivering new and better ways to get and stay healthy. Visit www.chpa.org.
About Council for Responsible Nutrition
The Council for Responsible Nutrition (CRN), founded in 1973 and based in Washington, D.C., is the leading trade association representing the dietary supplement and functional food industry. Bringing together manufacturers, ingredient suppliers, and service providers, CRN unites its member companies around a shared commitment to science, transparency, and responsible business practices—advancing a strong, credible marketplace that supports consumer health and industry growth. In an increasingly complex regulatory and media environment, CRN serves as the industry's front line—shaping science-based policy, defending market access, and countering misinformation. Through strategic advocacy, self-regulatory leadership, voluntary guidelines, and evidence-based communications, CRN ensures that responsible companies are recognized, protected, and positioned to innovate and compete. Learn more at crnusa.org and follow @CRN_Supplements on X and LinkedIn.

 Join AHPA
 Founded in 1982, the American Herbal Products Association (AHPA) is the national trade association and voice of the herbal products industry. AHPA is comprised of more than 350 member companies, consisting primarily of domestic and foreign companies doing business as growers, processors, manufacturers and marketers of herbs and herbal products as foods, dietary supplements, cosmetics, and non-prescription drugs, and also including companies that provide expert services to the herbal trade.
AHPA’s mission is to promote the responsible and sustainable commerce of herbal products to ensure that consumers have informed access to a wide variety of safe herbal goods. AHPA’s vision is for high quality herbal products to be readily accessible to and broadly used by consumers.
